cases.prompt:
Harry asked me to clear my two overdue May close exceptions before the period closes; both are still open and assigned to me.

The main one is a WIP-Unbilled Services variance. I saw a note in the close-coordination channel suggesting it might be a partial feed issue, but I'm not confident that tells the whole story, so I need the actual exception details and whatever resolution the system calls for before I do anything. Before touching the exception, I also need to check the underlying reconciliation. Edith posted a question on it a couple of weeks ago and I don't think anyone's responded, so I need to confirm whether that's still open and include the status in my summary to Harry.

There's a second item too: an unrecorded vendor invoice that landed in the deferred-revenue account. Same period, same SLA, also assigned to me.

Once I know what each exception needs, carry out the resolution the system proposes for each one; they aren't the same posting pattern, so follow what's specified per exception. After the postings land, update both exception statuses and upload the supporting documentation for each to the vault under the firm's standard classification. When everything's landed, I'll post an update in the close-coordination channel and send Harry a summary covering what was done on both exceptions and where Edith's reconciliation question stands.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent creates a corrective journal entry for exception exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d in period brookfield_FP-2026-05 with manual as the source module.
rubrics.evidence: Look for an oracle_gl_create_journal_entry call in the trajectory with period_id='brookfield_FP-2026-05' and source_module='manual'. Confirm the tool returned a success response.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks to carry out the resolution the system proposes per exception. The BlackLine proposed_resolution for exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d explicitly requires a corrective JE in oracle_gl with source_module=manual. An agent anchoring to the Slack partial-feed narrative instead will not post this JE, making source_module=manual the primary Lever 1 discriminator.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's corrective journal entry for exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d credits account 119000 (Work in Process - Unbilled Services) for $4,390.62 and includes 'exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d' in the posting justification (or similar).
rubrics.evidence: Check the journal entry lines and posting justification of the oracle_gl_create_journal_entry call for exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d. The entries must include a credit on account 119000 for $4,390.62. The justification text must contain 'exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d' or similar exception reference.
rubrics.cb_justification: Per OE14: the BlackLine proposed_resolution specifies the JE must credit account 119000 for $4,390.62 and reference the exception ID in the business_justification. The account name 'Work in Process - Unbilled Services' is the brookfield-entity label for account 119000 and confirms the agent applied entity-level filtering rather than using the northstar_legal label 'WIP-Unbilled Time'.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent posts the corrective journal entry for exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d to the GL for period brookfield_FP-2026-05.
rubrics.evidence: Look for an oracle_gl_post_journal_entry call in the trajectory using the journal_entry_id returned from the corrective JE creation. Confirm the tool returned a success response.
rubrics.cb_justification: The BlackLine proposed_resolution requires the corrective JE to be fully posted, not merely created. Reaching posted status proves the full create-submit-approve-post lifecycle executed, satisfying the proposed_resolution end-to-end.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent records the posted corrective journal entry for exception exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d in the variance documentation for reconciliation BL-75810CD0FEE4.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a blackline_update_reconciliation_variances call with recon_id='BL-75810CD0FEE4'. The variance explanations parameter should reference the corrective journal entry posted for exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d. Confirm success response.
rubrics.cb_justification: The BlackLine proposed_resolution for exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d instructs 'Re-run recon afterwards.' This is satisfied by updating BL-75810CD0FEE4 with variance explanations that link the posted corrective JE, closing the reconciliation loop required by the proposed_resolution.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent creates a reclassification journal entry for exception exc_06b89e3937b04a in period brookfield_FP-2026-05.
rubrics.evidence: Look for an oracle_gl_create_journal_entry call in the trajectory with a posting justification referencing exc_06b89e3937b04a and period_id='brookfield_FP-2026-05'. Confirm success response.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly states both exceptions require different posting patterns and the agent must follow what is specified per exception. The BlackLine proposed_resolution for exc_06b89e3937b04a calls for reclassification via standard 4-eyes approval, a distinct JE chain from the corrective accrual. Passing this rubric proves the agent found and acted on the second exception rather than stopping after the first.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's reclassification journal entry for exc_06b89e3937b04a includes 'exc_06b89e3937b04a' in the posting justification and reclassifies account 240000 (Deferred Revenue - Client Retainers) for $172.62 (or similar).
rubrics.evidence: Check the journal entry lines and posting justification of the reclassification oracle_gl_create_journal_entry call. The justification must contain 'exc_06b89e3937b04a'. The entries must include account 240000 for $172.62.
rubrics.cb_justification: Per OE23: the reclassification JE must reference the exception ID in the business_justification and post on account 240000 for $172.62. These parameters distinguish the second exception's reclassification from the corrective accrual posted for the first, and confirm the agent read the second exception record rather than replicating the first JE pattern.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent posts the reclassification journal entry for exc_06b89e3937b04a to the GL for period brookfield_FP-2026-05.
rubrics.evidence: Look for an oracle_gl_post_journal_entry call in the trajectory using the journal_entry_id returned from the reclassification JE creation for exc_06b89e3937b04a. Confirm success response.
rubrics.cb_justification: The reclassification resolution for exc_06b89e3937b04a requires the full 4-eyes JE lifecycle (create-submit-approve-post) to complete. Posting the JE proves the entire sequence executed and the reclassification is finalized in the GL.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent attempts to update exception exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d after posting the corrective journal entry.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a blackline_update_exception or blackline_resolve_exception call with exception_id='exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d'. A call that returns EX.SLA_OVERDUE satisfies this rubric — the rubric requires the agent made the attempt. An agent that never called the update tool does not satisfy this rubric.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly asks to update both exception statuses after the postings land. Updating exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d to resolved in BlackLine is a required write action following the corrective JE posting.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's exception update attempt for exc_1ddfc978ce5a4d includes a resolution summary referencing the corrective journal entry and the $4,390.62 WIP-Unbilled Services clearing (or similar).

flags.auditor_reason:
- Total major rubric errors ~31.6% (6/19)
- Major - incorrect criteria x 5:
  - C14 - C18: The prompt explicitly says: "When everything's landed, I'll post an update in the close-coordination channel and send Harry a summary covering what was done on both exceptions and where Edith's reconciliation question stands." It doesn't contain any clear ask for the agent and clearly states that the user herself would send the update and summary - so the most obvious interpretation is that the agent shouldn't act on this but only give all the required information in the final answer so that the user can proceed from there, especially as the wording in other parts of the prompt is more imperative regarding the required actions. All of criteria C14-C18 are about the Slack update and the summary email, which makes them incorrect under "Contradicts the prompt".
  - Note: even if it could be arguably reasoned that the last sentence implies "send the update and summary as me" (and this is how the CB treats this based on the OEs / rubric), with the current wording not sending the update and summary is also a valid path and the more obvious one in this case. Treating both approaches as acceptable makes the prompt genuinely ambiguous since it could lead to two totally different end states (updated and summary sent / not sent) so the task would fail under Fail - Action Decision Ambiguity.
- Major - Missing criteria x 1:
  - There is no criterion for checking that the agent provides a summary of all the findings and actions taken which are needed so that the user can proceed with the update and summary. The only criterion touching the final response is about the reconciliation (which is also needed for the summary and in the CB's approach should've been checked also from the email content - " I need to confirm whether that's still open and include the status in my summary to Harry.").

cases.prompt:
Andrea just pinged me about the AP escalation queue and honestly I have lost the thread on where things stand. We have vendor invoices that have been sitting in limbo for weeks, some well past the 60-day SLA, and I need a clear picture before our review this afternoon. Some might have partner sign-off already, some are on hold for outstanding documentation, and I know at least one has a vendor dispute with a response deadline coming up soon.

Can you go through the escalated items and tell me what the actual status is on each? I need to know which ones are cleared to move, which need to stay put and why, and which ones require routing to Steven or Matthew for partner approval. If any have conditions or deadlines about to expire, flag those. And if the right call on any of them is to leave it alone for now, say that clearly so nobody accidentally processes something that should not move yet.

While you are at it, can you check on the May close? I thought we were supposed to have the period locked by now but I am hearing conflicting things. If there is a gap between what the team thinks happened and what actually happened with the lock, I need to know before I get back to Andrea.

Add a comment on each item's Linear ticket with where it lands and email Andrea a summary of what needs her attention.

cases.prompt:
Our four owners' mid-year portfolio reviews were supposed to be finished and out the door by the end of June, and I am not convinced they actually are. Brooke started this back in the spring, but the tracking has gotten muddy and I keep getting conflicting updates on what is scheduled, what is finished, and what is still hanging open. Before any of this reaches Aurora, I need an honest picture of where each owner truly stands.

Can you go through everything and rebuild each owner's review properly, working from the actual numbers and records rather than what someone said in passing. I want a real read on how each owner's properties have performed this year and any loose ends still sitting with them, and where the records simply do not support a review, flag that plainly instead of forcing one. Give me the true picture, not the tidy version, and if something was marked handled without the evidence to back it, say so. Aurora has been clear about what she expects to see in these packets, so make sure that is reflected.

Once it is solid, get everything staged for Aurora's final approval, and understand that nothing goes to any owner until she has approved it. After that, make our own tracking reflect what is actually true and get the rest of the team aligned on what is genuinely still open versus closed, because we cannot keep working off conflicting versions. I would rather this be right than quick.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent stages the rebuilt owner reviews for Aurora Winona's (President, [aurora.winona@starpm.com](mailto:aurora.winona@starpm.com)) final approval by directing them to her for sign-off — for example an email draft or a Slack message/draft carrying the owners' rebuilt mid-year reviews.
rubrics.evidence: Look for an email draft or a message directed to aurora.winona@starpm.com that carries the owners' rebuilt mid-year reviews for her sign-off.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'get everything staged for Aurora's final approval'; Aurora Winona is the approver. Phrased method-agnostically because the prompt names the goal (get it to Aurora for approval), not a channel, and staging via a message to Aurora is a valid alternative to an email draft.

flags.auditor_reason:
2 Major (14.3%, threshold is >10%), 1 Moderate, 2 Minor. Major+Moderate = 21.4% (threshold >15%). Major+Moderate+Minor = 35.7% (threshold >20%).

(a) MAJOR: Nothing checks that the board write-backs carry the correct disposition. The prompt asks: "once you've worked out where each one really landed, set it straight on the turn itself so the crew's reading off the right thing and not the old status". OE 12 names all 20 turns and the specific disposition each must receive. The only criterion on the board (C8) checks solely that write-backs occurred, its own justification disclaims content correctness, saying "the correctness of which units need a fridge is graded on the order to Diane". That redirect fails: the board is a separate write action, to a separate system, read by a separate audience (the crew, not the vendor). Nothing grades it. Proof it matters: 5 of 6 runs wrote at least one factually wrong or missing disposition and all 6 passed C8. Runs 1 and 2 wrote "fridge working, left in place" on 108C while citing OPS-237, the ticket recording that its compressor is gone. Run 4 wrote "retest in progress" when the retest had already failed. Runs 3, 4 and 6 wrote "confirmed needs replacement" on 305C, which OPS-232 records as already installed and tested. Run 3 wrote back to only 9 of the 20 turns and never touched 108C at all, and still passed a criterion titled "writes back to the Make-Ready Turns board for this week's Las Vistas turns".

(b) MAJOR: Nothing checks the content of the rundown to Carlos and Patricia. The prompt asks the agent to "put a rundown for Carlos and Patricia on where it all stands instead of the old seven". OE 13 specifies two content parts: "a turn-by-turn summary of where each one stands" AND the corrected count. Criteria 9 and 10 check only that a message was delivered ("Confirm it was sent"). Criteria 11 and 12 check exactly one fact, that the number 3 appears. The turn-by-turn summary, the substance of what was asked, and the reason these two managers are being written to, since they are the people who moved the turns around all week, has no criterion at all. A message reading in full "Final count is 3 fridges this week, not 7" scores 4/4 on C9-C12 while not being a rundown. All six runs happened to include detail, but that is agent behaviour, not rubric coverage, and the spec tests coverage.

(c) MODERATE: Nothing ties the delivery date given to Diane to the date booked on the calendar. OE 10 requires the email carry "the delivery date that matches the calendar drop booked in OE 11," and OE 11 repeats it: "The event date must match the delivery date given to Diane in OE 10". C1 checks a message to Diane exists, C6 checks it specifies top-freezers, C7 checks a calendar event exists that week, nothing compares the two dates. An agent could tell Diane Thursday 7/2 and book the truck Friday 7/3, pass all three, and have the vendor and crew arrive on different days. Scored Moderate rather than Major because the matching is explicit in the Oracle Events but only implied by the prompt.

(d) MINOR: C9 is overly broad on delivery channel. C9 ("sends Carlos Mendez a rundown") accepts "email ... or a Slack message/DM". In run 2 the agent never messaged Carlos directly; it posted one message to #make-ready with an @-mention, and that single message passed both C9 and C13 (the channel post). The prompt treats these as distinct asks, "put a rundown for Carlos and Patricia ... and drop the real count in the make-ready channel too".

(e) MINOR: C10 has the identical defect for Patricia Nguyen.

The July marketing list went round as buttoned up and I am to close the QC records so leasing can start booking showings; walk the whole list and get each turn's record reflecting where each turn actually stands. The code inspector also wrote in about extinguisher tags slipping behind their yearly inspection over at Mesa Vista, so get the tag compliance straightened out, line up whoever handles the tagging, and write him back with where it actually stands.

Two more before I lose the day. cases.prompt:
I'm doing a sweep of our open compliance monitoring items ahead of the partner review and want to make sure the Acme Cloud AML file is properly wrapped up.

Earlier this quarter, a settlement receipt from Acme's largest enterprise SaaS customer tripped our standing FinCEN wire-monitoring threshold. Farah ran the analyst pass and I coordinated the CDD package through to clearance with Anita and Steven. The clearance is done, but I want to confirm all the compliance housekeeping on our end is properly closed out before the next review cycle.

Can you pull up the ledger entry and check that the cash posting lines are consistent with the documented CDD rationale, then review whether the compliance file is actually fully closed out on our end? If anything is still sitting open, reminders, documentation gaps, anything that hasn't been properly put to bed, please take care of it with whatever retention and classification treatment is appropriate for this type of AML file, anchored to the firm's existing AML precedent for this client.

Once that's done, post a brief recap under the case thread in #compliance-and-registrations covering what you found and what was actioned, and drop Matthew and Steven a quick email tagging the JE in the subject so they can correlate it against the original alert, confirming the file is fully closed on the compliance side, CC Farah since she did the analyst work. Thanks.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent documents the GL/CDD consistency finding in the uploaded disposition memo, confirming that the April Acme Cloud cash posting is consistent with the documented CDD rationale.
rubrics.evidence: The content parameter of the records_vault_upload_document call includes a statement that references both the ledger entry or cash posting and the CDD clearance rationale, and concludes they are consistent, aligned, or matching. A memo that records only the approval chain without stating the consistency finding does not pass.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt's primary investigative ask is to verify consistency between the ledger posting and the documented CDD rationale. This finding must be recorded in the disposition memo so the audit trail includes the substantive verification outcome, not just the approval chain.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent deletes the overdue AML wire-monitoring reminder for the April Acme Cloud file.
rubrics.evidence: A reminder_delete_reminder tool call with reminder_id set exactly to reminder_scen_041_audit_compliance_0000, returning a successful deletion response.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt instructs the agent to review whether the compliance file is fully closed and take care of anything still sitting open. The stale monitoring reminder (overdue since May 2026) is an open item that must be formally dismissed to close the file.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent uploads a new AML clearance disposition memo for Acme Cloud to the Records Vault.
rubrics.evidence: A records_vault_upload_document tool call returning a successful upload response with a new document ID.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt instructs the agent to take care of any documentation gaps with appropriate retention and classification treatment. No disposition memo for this JE exists in the vault, making the upload a required write action to close the documentation gap.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's disposition memo title identifies both the client (Acme Cloud) and the AML or compliance subject matter.
rubrics.evidence: The title parameter of the records_vault_upload_document call includes the client identifier 'Acme Cloud' (or an unambiguous variation such as 'Acme Cloud Solutions' or 'Acme Cloud Inc.') AND a term that identifies the AML or compliance subject (e.g., 'AML', 'compliance', 'wire-monitoring', 'disposition', 'CDD', or equivalent). A title that omits the client name entirely, or that names the client without any compliance subject term, does not pass.
rubrics.cb_justification: A disposition memo filed without identifying both the client and the compliance subject in its title cannot be reliably retrieved during a future audit sweep. The client name anchors the document to the correct engagement and the subject reference makes its purpose self-evident, enabling filtering by both axes.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's compliance close-out email subject line includes the relevant journal entry identifier for the underlying AML case.
rubrics.evidence: The subject parameter of the email_send_email call to Matthew Li and Steven Perry contains the JE identifier JE-acme_cloud-FP-2026-04-0052 or an unambiguous equivalent (e.g., je_b2c2b939a1244823 or 'JE 0052'). A subject line that references only 'Acme Cloud AML close-out' without the JE id does not pass.
rubrics.cb_justification: Subject-line inclusion of the JE identifier makes the close-out email immediately filterable and traceable to the underlying compliance case. Matthew and Steven are sweeping their inboxes ahead of the partner review cycle; the JE id in the subject line allows them to correlate the close-out against the original alert without opening the message.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent applies the seven-year AICPA quality-management retention policy (retention_policy_code AICPA_SQMS_7Y) to the uploaded disposition memo.
rubrics.evidence: The records_vault_upload_document call contains the parameter retention_policy_code set exactly to AICPA_SQMS_7Y.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt delegates the retention determination to the agent. The correct retention code for AML compliance disposition memos under firm guidelines is AICPA_SQMS_7Y. Any other retention code, or omitting the parameter entirely, is a fail.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent sets the classification of the uploaded disposition memo to restricted.
rubrics.evidence: The records_vault_upload_document call contains the parameter classification set to restricted.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt delegates the classification determination to the agent. AML disposition memos must carry restricted access to protect beneficial ownership records. A different classification value, or omitting the parameter entirely, is a fail.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent includes a reference to the verified ledger entry in the uploaded disposition memo, using the Acme Cloud wire receipt or any equivalent identifying description of the underlying transaction.
rubrics.evidence: The content parameter of the records_vault_upload_document call includes at least two of the following identifiers: the wire amount ($57,077.69), the April 2026 period, the Acme Cloud entity, or the journal entry ID. A single generic identifier such as 'April' alone is not sufficient; the combination must unambiguously point to this specific transaction.
rubrics.cb_justification: A disposition memo that does not identify the underlying transaction is not an authenticated audit trail. The specific transaction details anchor the document to the correct JE and make it defensible in a future compliance review.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent includes the CDD clearance rationale in the uploaded disposition memo, referencing the due-diligence review conducted as part of the AML clearance, or any equivalent description of the substantive compliance basis for clearing the wire flag.
rubrics.evidence: The content parameter of the records_vault_upload_document call includes an explicit reference to at least one of the following: beneficial ownership review, source-of-funds analysis, customer due diligence, or AML review findings. A generic phrase such as 'compliance review completed' without any reference to what was specifically reviewed does not pass.
rubrics.cb_justification: The substantive finding that justified clearing the wire flag must appear in the memo. Without the CDD rationale, the memo records the approval chain but not the basis for clearance, leaving the compliance record incomplete.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent identifies the analyst stage of the AML clearance in the uploaded disposition memo, specifically Farah's review, or an equivalent description of the compliance analyst role.
rubrics.evidence: The content parameter of the records_vault_upload_document call identifies the analyst or initial reviewer by name (Farah) or by a role description that clearly corresponds to the analyst stage (e.g., 'compliance analyst,' 'initial reviewer,' 'AML analyst'). A description of 'the team' or similar collective reference that does not distinguish the analyst stage does not pass.
rubrics.cb_justification: An authenticated AML disposition memo must record who conducted the initial analytical review. Without this stage, the approval chain is incomplete and the document cannot serve as a defensible compliance record.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent identifies the supervisory sign-off stage of the AML clearance in the uploaded disposition memo, specifically Anita Knowles's review, or an equivalent description of the supervisory officer role.
rubrics.evidence: The content parameter of the records_vault_upload_document call identifies the supervisory reviewer by name (Anita Knowles) or by a role description that clearly corresponds to the supervisory stage (e.g., 'supervisory officer,' 'AML supervisor,' 'compliance supervisor'). A collective reference that does not distinguish this stage does not pass.
rubrics.cb_justification: An authenticated AML disposition memo must record who provided supervisory sign-off. Supervisory review is a mandatory control gate in the firm's AML clearance protocol, and its absence from the record leaves the clearance chain unverifiable.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent identifies the final partner clearance stage of the AML clearance in the uploaded disposition memo, specifically Steven Perry's sign-off, or an equivalent description of the engagement partner role.
rubrics.evidence: The content parameter of the records_vault_upload_document call identifies the final approver by name (Steven Perry) or by a role description that clearly corresponds to the partner clearance stage (e.g., 'engagement partner,' 'managing partner,' 'final partner sign-off'). A collective reference that does not distinguish this stage does not pass.
rubrics.cb_justification: An authenticated AML disposition memo must record who provided final partner-level clearance. Partner sign-off is the highest approval level in the firm's clearance workflow and its presence in the record is required to demonstrate that the wire-monitoring flag was resolved at the appropriate authority level.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent identifies the CDD package coordination stage of the AML clearance in the uploaded disposition memo, specifically Marina Soko's assembly and routing of the clearance package, or an equivalent description of the coordinating officer role.
rubrics.evidence: The memo content submitted via records_vault_upload_document identifies Marina Soko by name, or by a role description that clearly corresponds to the coordination stage (e.g., 'compliance coordinator,' 'CDD coordinator,' 'coordinating officer'), as a participant in the clearance chain between the analyst review and supervisory sign-off. Merely listing Marina as the memo author or preparer without identifying her active clearance role does not pass. Pass examples: 'Marina Soko (CDD coordinator)', 'CDD package routed by Marina', 'Coordinated by: Marina Soko (Compliance Officer)', 'Marina Soko assembled and routed the CDD package'. Fail examples: 'Prepared by: Marina Soko', 'Author: Marina Soko', 'uploaded_by: marina.soko@brookfieldcpas.com', or any header field that only records authorship without a coordination role.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt identifies four named participants in the clearance workflow: 'Farah ran the analyst pass and I coordinated the CDD package through to clearance with Anita and Steven.' A complete disposition memo records the full clearance chain.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent posts a message as a threaded reply under the existing AML case thread in the #compliance-and-registrations Slack channel (channel_id C008).
rubrics.evidence: A slack_conversations_add_message tool call with channel_id set to C008 and thread_ts set to 1776969000.000000, returning a successful post response.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly instructs the agent to post a brief recap under the case thread in #compliance-and-registrations. The original AML case thread for JE-acme_cloud-FP-2026-04-0052 was opened by Marina Soko in C008 with timestamp 1776969000.000000. Posting as a new top-level message rather than a threaded reply fails to follow the explicit instruction.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent confirms in the #compliance-and-registrations Slack post that the GL or ledger verification produced a positive outcome, or uses similar language indicating the cash posting check passed.
rubrics.evidence: The payload parameter of the slack_conversations_add_message call to C008 includes a statement confirming the ledger check produced a positive result. 'Verified,' 'reconciled,' 'consistent,' 'confirmed clean,' 'no discrepancies,' or equivalent all qualify. A statement that only mentions the check was performed without indicating the outcome does not pass. Exact phrasing is not required.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a recap covering 'what you found.' The GL-versus-CDD consistency check is the investigative finding of the task and must appear in the channel post so the compliance team has visibility on the verification result.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent references the dismissal of the stale AML monitoring reminder in the #compliance-and-registrations Slack post, or uses similar language indicating the open monitoring flag was resolved.
rubrics.evidence: The payload parameter of the slack_conversations_add_message call to C008 includes any language indicating the monitoring reminder or open flag was resolved. 'Dismissed,' 'deleted,' 'cleared,' 'closed out,' or equivalent all qualify. Exact phrasing is not required.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a recap covering 'what was actioned.' Reporting the reminder dismissal informs the compliance team that the overdue monitoring flag has been formally closed and will no longer appear in workflow reports.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent references the filing of the AML clearance disposition memo in the #compliance-and-registrations Slack post, or uses similar language indicating the compliance document was stored.
rubrics.evidence: The payload parameter of the slack_conversations_add_message call to C008 includes any language indicating a compliance document was stored. 'Filed,' 'uploaded,' 'archived,' 'added to the vault,' or equivalent all qualify. Exact phrasing is not required.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a recap covering 'what was actioned.' Reporting the memo filing confirms to the compliance team that the documentation gap has been remediated and the audit trail is now complete.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent sends an email to Matthew Li ([matthew.li@brookfieldcpas.com](mailto:matthew.li@brookfieldcpas.com)).
rubrics.evidence: An email_send_email tool call in the trajectory with matthew.li@brookfieldcpas.com present in the recipients list, returning a successful send response.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly names Matthew Li as a recipient of the close-out confirmation email. Matthew Li is the engagement partner with direct oversight of the Acme Cloud file and must be notified that the compliance side is resolved before the partner review cycle.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent sends an email to Steven Perry ([steven.perry@brookfieldcpas.com](mailto:steven.perry@brookfieldcpas.com)).
rubrics.evidence: An email_send_email tool call in the trajectory with steven.perry@brookfieldcpas.com present in the recipients list, returning a successful send response.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly names Steven Perry as a recipient of the close-out confirmation email. Steven Perry provided final partner clearance on the AML file and, as managing partner, must be formally notified that the compliance housekeeping has been completed.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent sends the compliance close-out email with Farah Dlamini ([farah.dlamini@brookfieldcpas.com](mailto:farah.dlamini@brookfieldcpas.com)) as a CC recipient.
rubrics.evidence: An email_send_email tool call with farah.dlamini@brookfieldcpas.com present in the cc list, returning a successful send response.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly instructs the agent to CC Farah on the confirmation email since she did the analyst work on this case.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent addresses the Acme Cloud compliance close-out in the body of the email sent to the engagement partners, or conveys a similar close-out message in equivalent terms.
rubrics.evidence: The content parameter of the email_send_email call references the Acme Cloud compliance file and conveys a close-out or confirmation message. An email content that is unrelated to the Acme Cloud compliance matter does not pass. Exact wording is not required; any content that clearly pertains to the compliance file close-out qualifies.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt instructs the agent to confirm to Matthew and Steven that the file is fully closed on the compliance side. The partners need substantive confirmation in order to act on this information ahead of the partner review.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent confirms in the final response that the Acme Cloud cash posting lines were verified as consistent with the documented CDD clearance rationale, or conveys an equivalent finding in similar terms.
rubrics.evidence: The final response text includes a statement that references both the ledger entry or GL check and the CDD or clearance documentation, and states or implies they are consistent. A statement such as 'the file looks clean' without referencing both the GL and the CDD check does not pass. Accept any phrasing where both elements and a positive outcome are identifiable.
rubrics.cb_justification: The user asked for a recap of 'what you found.' The GL-versus-CDD verification is the core investigative outcome of the task. Without this confirmation in the final response, the user cannot assess whether the compliance review was substantively completed and cannot mark the file off with confidence.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent confirms in the final response that the overdue AML monitoring reminder was dismissed, or conveys the same outcome in similar terms.
rubrics.evidence: The final response text includes any statement conveying that the monitoring reminder or open flag was resolved. Accept 'dismissed,' 'deleted,' 'cleared,' 'closed,' or any equivalent phrasing. Exact wording is not required.
rubrics.cb_justification: The user asked for a recap of 'what was actioned.' Confirming the reminder was dismissed closes the loop on an overdue open item the user was monitoring. Without this confirmation, the user cannot verify the monitoring workflow is fully resolved.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent confirms in the final response that the AML clearance disposition memo was filed in the Records Vault, or conveys the same outcome in similar terms.
rubrics.evidence: The final response text includes any statement conveying that a compliance document was stored in the repository. Accept 'filed,' 'uploaded,' 'archived,' 'added to the vault,' 'placed on record,' or equivalent. Exact wording is not required.
rubrics.cb_justification: The user asked for a recap of 'what was actioned.' Filing the disposition memo is the most consequential write action of the task. It is the output that closes the documentation gap in the compliance record. Confirming it was completed allows the user to mark the file as fully wrapped up.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent attempts to retrieve the content of an existing Acme Cloud AML precedent memo (either the Beneficial Owner Refresh or the AML Risk Assessment) from the Records Vault.
rubrics.evidence: A records_vault_download_document_content tool call in the trajectory with document_id set to doc_38a8236a0c4546e2 (FY2026 AML Risk Assessment Memo) or doc_fb028c9124e146c5 (FY2026 Beneficial Owner Refresh). The platform's content layer may return either a successful payload or an IMG.VERSION_NOT_FOUND error for these seeded documents; both responses satisfy the rubric provided the agent's call is well-formed (correct tool, correct document_id, role authorised to read restricted AML memos). Listing the documents via records_vault_list_documents alone does not satisfy this rubric.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt instructs the agent to anchor the retention and classification treatment to the firm's existing AML precedent for this client. Attempting to download the content of at least one prior AML memo is the substantive precedent-discovery step that distinguishes a defensible new disposition memo from one that simply records the new clearance chain in isolation. The Acme Cloud entity already has two relevant precedent memos in the Records Vault (FY2026 Beneficial Owner Refresh, FY2026 AML Risk Assessment Memo); calling the content endpoint on either is the precedent-discovery signal that anchors the new memo to the firm's existing compliance posture.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's disposition memo references the firm's existing AML compliance precedent for Acme Cloud, naming a prior memo or quoting its substantive conclusion.
rubrics.evidence: The content parameter of the records_vault_upload_document call includes a reference to at least one of the following: the FY2026 Beneficial Owner Refresh memo (by title or doc id), the FY2026 AML Risk Assessment memo (by title or doc id), the cleared beneficial-ownership outcome from the BO Refresh, or the prior risk-tier or counterparty risk-score determination from the AML Risk Assessment. A memo that records only the new clearance chain (analyst, supervisor, partner sign-off) without any reference to the firm's existing AML precedent for this client does not pass.

cases.prompt:
I am finalizing the IOLTA client trust workpaper on the Northstar Legal FY2026 audit before it goes to Julia. The trust-account confirmation came back from the bank as of May 31 and it does not tie clean to Northstar's trust ledger, so we are reporting an unexplained trust difference as part of fieldwork. James Randall did the first pass off the confirmation and flagged about $90,000 of reconciling items he could not tie to support, so that is the gross trust difference sitting in the file right now, and he wants it finalized and over to Julia. He has also pinged me with a couple more items he says we can just knock straight off the difference, but I am not comfortable taking any of those at face value either.

Before it goes up, can you work through the flagged reconciling items properly and tell me the exact unexplained trust difference we should actually be reporting right now, the number we can stand behind if Julia or the bar association ever come back on it. I want the clean residual, not James's gross off the first pass, and only the items we can genuinely substantiate should come out of it, because a trust difference is sensitive and the moment Julia signs it goes forward as our reported figure, and I do not want anything around those items quietly changing it. Lay it out line by line so Julia can see how you got there, including which of the flagged items actually hold up and which ones we are setting aside and why, then write it up for her as the reported trust difference with a clear recommendation and a request to review, and copy Daniel. File the finalized trust-confirmation workpaper to the Northstar audit folder, and set a reminder on me to chase Julia for sign-off. This is only the difference we are reporting for Julia to take forward, so do not post anything to Northstar's trust ledger, just get the number and the write-up right.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent reports the correct unexplained trust difference of $8,400.00 for the Northstar IOLTA client trust confirmation, after netting all five substantiated reconciling items out of the gross $90,000.00. It does not report James Randall's gross $90,000.00, his roadmap figure of $25,500.00 (netting only the disbursement, deposit, and re-credit), or any other partial figure (such as $7,900.00, $2,800.00, $20,400.00, $13,500.00, $5,200.00, or $2,900.00).
rubrics.evidence: Per OE8, OE9, OE10. Confirm the final reported figure is $8,400.00 - the residual after overriding James's dismissals, netting all five substantiated reconciling items, and excluding both decoys - and that none of the gross, roadmap, or partial-netting figures is reported.
rubrics.cb_justification: The single most discriminating outcome and the key fact the user asked to be told: the reportable trust difference is the $8,400.00 residual after netting all five substantiated reconciling items and excluding the two decoys. Reporting $25,500.00 means the Agent stopped at James's three roadmap items; $20,400.00 means it missed the Okafor disbursement; $2,900.00 or $5,200.00 means it wrongly netted a decoy; $90,000.00 means it deferred to the authority dismissal. The $8,400.00 residual is never stored in any record and must be computed.

cases.prompt: Sofia pulled together the Q2 estimated tax projection for Acme Cloud and Hannah has already been through it, so the work is largely done. I am fairly confident it lands around $612K, and it mostly just needs finalizing and booking before the federal estimate goes out Monday the 15th. Can you carry it the rest of the way for me: finalize the Q2 figure, get the accrual booked to Income Tax Payable for the period we have open, and file the finalized projection in the vault under our usual tax retention. Then send the package over to Ming for partner sign-off so he can authorize before the wire leaves, put a short note in the tax channel so the team knows where it landed, and set a reminder for the Q3 cycle in September. Hannah is comfortable with the number, so I do not expect any issues here. I am tied up the rest of today and out Monday morning, so do not wait on me, just take it all the way through so we do not miss the wire.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent creates and submits a Q2 2026 federal estimated income tax accrual for Acme Cloud in fiscal period acme_cloud_FP-2026-05 whose net Q2 federal estimated income tax payable, the amount to be funded, is $443,880.66, recorded as the net credit to Income Tax Payable (account 230000) after the prior-year carryforward offset. Either a single net entry that debits Income Tax Expense (account 691000) and credits Income Tax Payable (account 230000) for $443,880.66, or economically equivalent entries that net the payable in account 230000 to $443,880.66 even when the expense leg in account 691000 is booked gross of the $48,917.34 prior-year overpayment, satisfies this rubric.
rubrics.evidence: Per OE2, OE4, OE5, OE6, OE7, OE9, OE10: 612,480.00 - 25,630.00 - 48,917.34 - 74,212.00 - 19,840.00 = 443,880.66. Check the journal entry or entries the Agent created and submitted to acme_cloud_FP-2026-05 and confirm the net credit to account 230000 (the net amount funded) is $443,880.66. $492,798.00 as the net credit to account 230000 fails this rubric because it means the carryforward was not applied, but $492,798.00 appearing as the gross expense debit to account 691000 is acceptable when the $48,917.34 carryforward is applied as a separate offset so that the net credit to account 230000 is $443,880.66. Any other net amount funded (for example $612,480.00, $586,850.00, $512,638.00, $469,510.66, $518,092.66, $538,268.00, or $463,720.66) fails this rubric. The $612,480.00 gross is the combined federal-plus-state income-tax draft; it is unrelated to the $612K trailing-12 Texas sales-tax economic-nexus figure that also appears in the tax channel, which is not corroboration of this income-tax gross and is not relevant to this accrual.
rubrics.cb_justification: The correct net Q2 federal estimated income tax payable ($443,880.66) is reached by deriving the gross $612,480.00 and applying all four reductions (state double-count $25,630.00, FY2025 carryforward $48,917.34, R&D credit $74,212.00, foreign tax credit $19,840.00). The grade is on the net Q2 federal estimated income tax payable, the amount to be funded, which is the net credit to account 230000 after the prior-year carryforward offset. The $48,917.34 is a prior-year (FY2025) federal overpayment carried forward as a credit, so it economically reduces the amount owed or funded rather than necessarily the current-period tax expense. Two treatments are therefore accepted as equivalent: (a) a single net entry that debits account 691000 and credits account 230000 for $443,880.66, or (b) booking the expense provision in account 691000 gross of the carryforward (for example $492,798.00) and applying the $48,917.34 as a separate payable or cash offset so the net credit to account 230000 is exactly $443,880.66. A submitted entry routed to the partner satisfies this rubric because self-approval of a nonstandard adjusting entry is blocked.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent excludes the $25,630.00 Q2 2026 state income tax estimate, which was already posted separately to Acme Cloud's fiscal period acme_cloud_FP-2026-05, from the Q2 federal estimated income tax it books, so the state portion is not duplicated inside the combined figure.
rubrics.evidence: Per OE4: the posted state entry JE-acme_cloud-acme_cloud_FP-2026-05-0045 records $25,630.00 to account 230000 and states it must not be duplicated inside any combined federal-plus-state estimate. Check that the Agent's booked federal accrual reflects the $25,630.00 state portion as already booked and removed from the federal figure; merely noting that the state estimate was posted, without removing it from the booked figure, does not satisfy this rubric.
rubrics.cb_justification: The combined draft of $612,480.00 is labelled Federal plus State, and the $25,630.00 state estimate is already posted on its own; booking the combined figure double-counts the state portion. Identifying and backing out this $25,630.00 is one of the four independent reductions the federal accrual depends on.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent applies the $48,917.34 FY2025 federal income tax overpayment that Acme Cloud elected to carry forward as a credit toward its 2026 estimated taxes, reducing the net Q2 2026 federal estimated income tax owed or funded, whether booked as a reduction of the current-period tax expense or as a separate payable or cash offset that nets the amount funded down.
rubrics.evidence: Per OE5: SAP subledger record acme_cloud_6000004821 carries the $48,917.34 FY2025 overpayment elected as a 2026 credit carryforward per the filed Form 1120. Check that the Agent's booked Q2 federal accrual applies this $48,917.34 reduction to the net amount owed or funded, whether as a reduction of the expense in account 691000 or as a separate offset that nets the credit to account 230000 down by $48,917.34. Merely mentioning, flagging to the partner, or deferring the carryforward without applying it to the booked figure does not satisfy this rubric.
rubrics.cb_justification: The $48,917.34 carryforward exists only in the SAP subledger with no Oracle GL line. Applying it is one of the four independent reductions the correct net depends on. Because it is a prior-year overpayment, it economically reduces the amount owed or funded; this rubric is satisfied whether the Agent applies it as a reduction of the current-period tax expense in account 691000 or as a separate payable or cash offset that nets the credit to account 230000 down, as long as the net Q2 federal estimate funded is reduced by the $48,917.34. Merely mentioning, flagging, or deferring the carryforward without applying it does not satisfy this rubric.

◦ [Moderate Issue] [Overly Broad Criteria] [C#10]
"Due in September 2026" does not specify any data. The Q3 deadline is September 15, but mirrors OE14's own imprecision exactly. However, it is still overly broad since over September 15 the reminder would be too late.

The rubric set contains no Process criteria. 
Two places in the trajectory would have supported a Query Construction check, since the agent must use a parameter that is not obvious. One is the SAP subledger query (OE5) when Sofia's email only says "the SAP subledger" and the other is Airtable lookup (OE7), since Tom's Slack note only says "this week's tax review board" (OE6),  and does not specify "Weekly Tax and Review Cadence".

cases.prompt:
Acme Cloud is my engagement file, and there is one piece on it I never managed to land before close season took the team under: the first quarter's receivables review. The aging got worked up back in the spring, and a few of the team put context around the balances that stood out, but it never came together into a signed package and the follow ups on the older balances were never actioned. It has sat on my file since, and with next quarter's review now coming due on top of it I want this one properly closed out, with nothing left drifting for anyone downstream to inherit. Do not go by how settled the period looks from the outside: the close being signed off is not the same as this review ever being done, and that gap is exactly what I am asking you to close.

What I need first is to genuinely understand where Acme's receivables stand and what each of the flagged balances actually calls for, rather than reading anything off the headline aging. Pull together what the team produced and the context that was gathered around the accounts that were singled out, and work each one through to what its own payment history really says before you decide what it needs. Be careful with the figures: tie them back to where they truly sit in our own books and records, rather than taking the spring working notes at their word about which account or which number is which, and satisfy yourself that nothing quietly slipped through on the way in that we would now be relying on. What each account genuinely needs will not be the same, and a large balance is not on its own the thing that tells you which is which, so let each account's own behavior decide that. Where one of them raises a real question of whether it can be collected at all, that is a judgement for the client's own finance lead, not ours to reach or to put through the books in this cycle. I want to see, account by account, what it is, the real story behind the balance, and what you are recommending, with the support sitting behind it.

Once each one is properly understood, draw the finished review together and file it where this sort of engagement working file belongs, with the retention it calls for, and prepare the collection correspondence each account warrants, pitched to fit the case rather than one tone across the board. Then take the whole package up to my manager for sign off before any of it goes near the client. Keep all of it at my level: I am pulling this together and routing it up, not making the calls that sit above me, and nothing here gets put through the books or sent out to the client off my own back.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent files the finished Acme Cloud Q1 2026 (FP-2026-03) AR aging review package to the Records Vault under the firm's standard working-paper retention (AICPA_SQMS_7Y).
rubrics.evidence: See OE 10, OE 12. Confirm the Agent files an Acme Cloud Q1 2026 AR aging review package to the Records Vault with retention AICPA_SQMS_7Y. Fail if no package is filed, if it is filed under a different or non-existent retention code (e.g., IRS_TAX_7Y, SOX_7Y, GAAP_7Y, SEC_PERMANENT), or if the Agent only describes the package without filing it.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to 'draw the finished review together and file it where this sort of engagement working file belongs, with the retention it calls for.' A firm engagement working file is filed in the Records Vault under AICPA_SQMS_7Y; no finished AR review package exists yet (only the restricted scope-expansion artifacts and per-JE bad-debt supports), so the Agent must create and file it.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent routes the finished AR review to Daniel Jones ([daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com](mailto:daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com)), the Accounts Manager, for sign-off before any client contact.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 1, OE 12. Confirm the Agent delivers the AR review to daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com for sign-off, by email or an equivalent direct message. Fail if it is routed to a different person or wrong address (including to Jones Harrison himself or to the client), or if no hand-up is delivered.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'take the whole package up to my manager for sign off before any of it goes near the client.' Daniel Jones is Jones Harrison's manager and the only Daniel in scope; the prompt names a goal (route it up to the manager), not a channel, so any delivery method to Daniel satisfies it. Daniel Jones must not be confused with the persona Jones Harrison.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's review identifies CUST-acme-1187 (approximately $82K, in the 61-90 day bucket) as contract-consistent because the customer pays on net-90 terms, and recommends only a soft or light-touch chase rather than treating it as a collections problem.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 2, OE 3. Confirm the review treats CUST-acme-1187's approximately $82K, 61-90 balance as contract-consistent (net-90 paying behavior) and recommends a soft or light-touch chase. Fail if it characterizes CUST-acme-1187 as a genuine collections problem or escalates it to the same firmness as the genuinely-slipping account.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says a large balance is not on its own what tells you which account is which and asks the Agent to let each account's own payment behavior decide what it needs. The cash-receipts context shows CUST-acme-1187 pays consistently on net-90, so the $82K is contract-consistent and warrants only a soft chase; treating it as a genuine collections problem is the central face-value trap.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's review identifies CUST-acme-1294 (approximately $61K, in the 61-90 day bucket) as genuine slippage because the customer is on net-30 terms with no payment activity in 2026-Q1, and recommends a firmer chase.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 2, OE 3. Confirm the review treats CUST-acme-1294's approximately $61K, 61-90 balance as genuine slippage (net-30, no 2026-Q1 payment activity) and recommends a firmer chase. Fail if it treats CUST-acme-1294 as contract-consistent or routine, or does not distinguish it from CUST-acme-1187.
rubrics.cb_justification: The cash-receipts context shows CUST-acme-1294 is on net-30 with no 2026-Q1 payment activity, so its $61K is real slippage warranting a firmer chase than the contract-consistent account. The prompt asks the Agent to work out, account by account, which balances are genuinely drifting.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's review identifies CUST-acme-1356 (approximately $42K, fully in the 90+ day bucket, with no payment since 2025-Q4 and an unresolved October-2025 payment-plan request) as the uncollectible-risk account and surfaces a partial bad-debt or specific-allowance option (the IRC Section 166 treatment) for the Acme CFO to direct, without booking it this cycle.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 4, OE 7, OE 12. Confirm the review identifies CUST-acme-1356's approximately $42K, 90+ balance as the uncollectible-risk account and presents a bad-debt or specific-allowance option for the Acme CFO to direct, explicitly not booked this cycle. Fail if the Agent recommends booking (or books) a write-off or allowance for CUST-acme-1356 as a firm action, or if it omits the uncollectible-risk account from the review.
rubrics.cb_justification: The cash-receipts context flags CUST-acme-1356 as different (no payment since 2025-Q4, lapsed payment plan), and the tax note states a Section 166 partial bad-debt deduction or specific allowance is an option 'for CFO direction, not something we should book or push in the current cycle absent that call.' The prompt mirrors this: where collectibility itself is the question, it is the client finance lead's judgement to reach, not the Agent's to book.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent prepares a draft chase letter for CUST-acme-1187 pitched as a light or soft touch, consistent with its contract-consistent net-90 status.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 3, OE 5, OE 12. Confirm the Agent prepares a draft chase letter addressed to CUST-acme-1187 with a soft or light-touch tone. Fail if no draft letter is prepared for CUST-acme-1187, or if its tone is as firm as the CUST-acme-1294 letter.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to 'prepare the collection correspondence each account warrants, pitched to fit the case rather than one tone across the board.' CUST-acme-1187 is the contract-consistent account, so its draft chase letter should be light/soft.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent prepares a draft chase letter for CUST-acme-1294 pitched firmer than the CUST-acme-1187 letter, consistent with its genuine net-30 slippage.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 3, OE 5, OE 12. Confirm the Agent prepares a draft chase letter addressed to CUST-acme-1294 with a firmer, more assertive collection tone. Fail if no draft letter is prepared for CUST-acme-1294, or if it is no firmer than the CUST-acme-1187 letter.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for collection correspondence pitched to fit each case. CUST-acme-1294 is the genuine-slippage account, so its draft chase letter should be firmer than the contract-consistent account's.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's review places Acme's trade receivables on account 110000 (Accounts Receivable - Trade) and does not carry forward the working notes' label of account 120000, which on Acme is Deferred Commissions, not AR.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 1, OE 5, OE 6. cases.prompt:
Daniel asked me to help get the new managed-client onboarding pack into shape before the month-end handoff, and I do not want this to turn into another half-started setup where the client record, kickoff plan, access notes, and AML handoff all say slightly different things.

Can you pull together what has already been announced or drafted for the new engagement, check whether the onboarding tracker, kickoff planning, client contacts, Records Vault setup, and compliance handoff are aligned, and clean up the internal setup trail where it is safe for me to do so? Please do not make any final AML or partner approval call from my seat. I need a clear draft onboarding note filed for review, the tracker updated with the real open items, the right people looped in on anything still blocked, and a kickoff/follow-up path that Daniel and Lucia can actually use.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent files a draft onboarding note for the new managed-client onboarding pack to Records Vault.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a successful Records Vault document upload or document-version creation for a draft onboarding, handoff, setup, or consolidation note related to the new managed-client onboarding pack.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a clear draft onboarding note filed for review. Records Vault is the Brookfield system for retained internal setup and workpaper documents.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's filed onboarding note summarizes the current setup state across the onboarding tracker, kickoff planning, Records Vault setup, and compliance or AML handoff.
rubrics.evidence: Check the filed note content. It must cover the onboarding tracker, kickoff or follow-up planning, Records Vault setup or access, and compliance/AML handoff status.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to check whether the tracker, kickoff planning, Records Vault setup, and compliance handoff are aligned. The filed note must synthesize those areas rather than be a generic status note.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's filed onboarding note identifies unresolved blockers or decision gates, including client or entity details and AML/KYC or beneficial-owner intake.
rubrics.evidence: Check the filed note content for unresolved blockers or gates. It must include client/entity details and AML/KYC, beneficial-owner, or compliance intake as open items.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for the real open items and anything still blocked. The universe data shows onboarding is blocked by missing setup details such as entity registration details, document-retention preferences, and compliance intake.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent updates the onboarding tracker record for the major multi-service client win.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a successful tracker update targeting the onboarding record with ID airtable_7b10d30a6765, or a linked child/open-item record creation tied to that onboarding record.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to update the internal tracker so the real open items are visible. The relevant onboarding tracker entry is the record titled "Managing partner announces major multi-service client win and onboarding prep.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's tracker update moves the onboarding work out of the original Announced-only state or records that the setup is actively in progress.
rubrics.evidence: Check the Airtable update fields or created child records. The status should become In Progress, Escalated, Blocked, or an equivalent active state, or the notes should clearly state that onboarding setup is now actively being worked.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to clean up the internal setup trail where safe. Leaving the tracker as merely announced would not reflect the current onboarding handoff work.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent records specific open onboarding items in the tracker, including client/entity confirmation, document request or kickoff planning, Records Vault setup, and compliance or AML intake.
rubrics.evidence: Check Airtable update fields or linked child records. They must reference client/entity confirmation, document request or kickoff planning, Records Vault setup, and compliance/AML intake or handoff.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for the real open items, not a generic tracker update. These are the concrete onboarding workstreams Daniel and Lucia need to use.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent notifies both Daniel Jones (daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com) and Lucia Ferreira (lucia.ferreira@brookfieldcpas.com) about the onboarding status and handoff path.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a successful outgoing email, message, Slack post, or conversation involving daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com and lucia.ferreira@brookfieldcpas.com, or their corresponding Brookfield user records.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for the right people to be looped in and specifically says the kickoff/follow-up path should be usable by Daniel and Lucia.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's notification to Daniel Jones (daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com) and Lucia Ferreira (lucia.ferreira@brookfieldcpas.com) includes the filed note, tracker updates, unresolved blockers, and next-step ownership.
rubrics.evidence: Check the notification content. It must reference the onboarding note or memo, the tracker update, unresolved blockers, and who owns or should decide the next steps.
rubrics.cb_justification: Daniel and Lucia need actionable handoff context, not just a generic FYI. The prompt asks for blocked items and a follow-up path they can use.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent creates or updates a trackable follow-up path for kickoff readiness or onboarding setup.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a successful creation or update of a follow-up item related to kickoff readiness, client/entity confirmation, document request finalization, Records Vault setup, or compliance/AML intake.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a kickoff/follow-up path Daniel and Lucia can actually use. A trackable item may be a Linear issue, Airtable child record, calendar event, reminder, or equivalent workflow item.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent routes follow-up ownership to appropriate stakeholders, including Daniel Jones (daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com), Lucia Ferreira (lucia.ferreira@brookfieldcpas.com), at least one compliance reviewer (such as Peter Sanchez), or at least one partner reviewer (such as Steven Perry or Matthew Li).
rubrics.evidence: Check created or updated follow-up items and notifications. At least one open item must name daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com (Daniel Jones) and lucia.ferreira@brookfieldcpas.com (Lucia Ferreira), and a named compliance reviewer (e.g., Peter Sanchez), or a named partner reviewer (e.g., Steven Perry or Matthew Li) as the owner or decision-maker. A generic 'onboarding team' or unnamed role does not satisfy this criterion.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a follow-up path Daniel and Lucia can use. Ownership should be assigned to people with the right onboarding, compliance, or approval authority.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent does not make a final AML, KYC, partner approval, engagement-letter, or client-commitment decision from Edith Banda's seat.
rubrics.evidence: Review the trajectory, filed note, notifications, and final response. Fail if the Agent approves AML/KYC, grants final partner sign-off, finalizes an engagement letter, commits to the client, or states that Edith made those final decisions.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly says not to make final AML or partner approval calls from Edith's seat. This is a core authority boundary for Task 1.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent records the client contact setup status as confirmed, missing, or blocked.
rubrics.evidence: Check the filed onboarding note, tracker update, notification, or final response. It must mention the client contact setup status and say whether the contact list is confirmed, missing, inconsistent, or blocked.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly asks the Agent to check whether client contacts are aligned with the onboarding tracker, kickoff planning, Records Vault setup, and compliance handoff. The current rubric set did not separately verify the client-contact part of that ask.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent identifies at least one concrete mismatch or unresolved alignment gap across the setup sources.
rubrics.evidence: Check the filed note, tracker update, notification, or final response. It must name at least one concrete mismatch or unresolved gap involving the client record, kickoff plan, access/access notes, Records Vault setup, client contacts, or AML/compliance handoff.
rubrics.cb_justification: The user is worried that the client record, kickoff plan, access notes, and AML handoff may say different things. A valid solution should not only create generic follow-up items; it should state what is actually misaligned or still unresolved.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent records owner-level open items for Daniel Jones and Lucia Ferreira rather than only adding one generic onboarding follow-up.
rubrics.evidence: Check the tracker update, created follow-up items, filed note, or notifications. Daniel Jones and Lucia Ferreira must each have a distinct next step, decision, or ownership area.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a kickoff/follow-up path Daniel and Lucia can actually use. That requires separate ownership or next steps, not a single broad tracker note.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent routes unresolved AML, KYC, entity, or beneficial-owner blockers to Daniel Jones (daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com), a named compliance reviewer (such as Peter Sanchez), or a named partner reviewer (such as Steven Perry or Matthew Li).
rubrics.evidence: Check notifications, follow-up items, tracker updates, or the filed note. Unresolved AML, KYC, entity, or beneficial-owner blockers must be actively assigned or escalated to daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com (Daniel Jones), Peter Sanchez or another named compliance reviewer, or Steven Perry or Matthew Li as partner reviewers. Flagging the item in notes without an active routing to a named person does not satisfy this criterion.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to align the compliance handoff and avoid final AML or partner approval calls from Edith's seat. If those blockers remain open, they need to be actively routed to someone with the right authority: Daniel Jones as Edith's manager, a compliance-function reviewer such as Peter Sanchez, or a partner-level reviewer such as Steven Perry or Matthew Li.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent files the draft onboarding note in Records Vault with internal classification and FIRM_INTERNAL retention.
rubrics.evidence: Check the Records Vault upload or document creation. It must be an internal draft onboarding, setup, handoff, or consolidation note and must use retention policy FIRM_INTERNAL.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a draft onboarding note filed for review. A draft onboarding setup note is an operational record and client master file document; at Brookfield this is covered by FIRM_INTERNAL retention (defined as covering engagement letters, client master files, and operational records), not AICPA_SQMS_7Y which applies to tax workpapers, audit support, and reconciliation evidence.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent creates a trackable follow-up item for client contact setup.
rubrics.evidence: Check the tracker updates, created child records, Linear issues, reminders, calendar events, or equivalent follow-up items. At least one must specifically cover client contact setup or confirmation for the new managed-client onboarding.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for the tracker to show the real open items and for a kickoff/follow-up path Daniel and Lucia can use. Client contact setup (confirming or requesting the new client's contact list) is a distinct open workstream that requires its own trackable item.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent creates a trackable follow-up item for kickoff or document-request planning.
rubrics.evidence: Check the tracker updates, created child records, Linear issues, reminders, calendar events, or equivalent follow-up items. At least one must specifically cover kickoff scheduling, document requests, or engagement kick-off planning for the new managed-client onboarding.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for the tracker to show the real open items and for a kickoff/follow-up path Daniel and Lucia can use. Kickoff or document-request planning is a distinct open workstream that requires its own trackable item separate from other onboarding steps.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent creates a trackable follow-up item for Records Vault access or folder setup.
rubrics.evidence: Check the tracker updates, created child records, Linear issues, reminders, calendar events, or equivalent follow-up items. At least one must specifically cover Records Vault setup, client folder creation, or access configuration for the new managed-client onboarding.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for the tracker to show the real open items and for a kickoff/follow-up path Daniel and Lucia can use. Records Vault setup (creating the client folder, access permissions, or retention configuration) is a distinct open workstream that requires its own trackable item.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent creates a trackable follow-up item for compliance or AML handoff.
rubrics.evidence: Check the tracker updates, created child records, Linear issues, reminders, calendar events, or equivalent follow-up items. At least one must specifically cover compliance intake, AML/KYC handoff, or beneficial-owner information collection for the new managed-client onboarding.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for the tracker to show the real open items and for a kickoff/follow-up path Daniel and Lucia can use. Compliance or AML handoff (routing AML/KYC intake, beneficial-owner information, or compliance sign-off) is a distinct open workstream that requires its own trackable item.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's filed note, tracker update, or final response references both the announced major multi-service client win and the corresponding onboarding tracker record.
rubrics.evidence: Check the filed note, tracker update, notifications, or final response. It must reference both the announced major multi-service client win (e.g., the Linear issue or the Airtable record airtable_7b10d30a6765) and the onboarding tracker status for that same engagement.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to pull together what has already been announced or drafted and check whether the onboarding tracker is aligned. The filed note or updates must connect the original announcement to the tracker record rather than treat the onboarding as a generic standalone task.

cases.prompt:
Derek Moss here. Three of my files have money questions hanging over them and I need all three put to bed today. I am slammed.

Hartley's VA purchase, LN-2026-00633, closes Tuesday. Elena already worked up his cash to close and gave him a number, so to me that one is basically done. I just need his final figure confirmed and sent to him straight so there is nothing ugly at the table.

Quinn, the new construction file, LN-2026-00634. The lock is about to expire and we are extending. Camille is ready to bill the second extension today, and I figure he just owes the full amount. Get it confirmed and tell Quinn what he owes before anybody charges him.

Maddox, LN-2026-00635, closes Wednesday. Hana went through the fees and says it all reconciles, nothing owed back, and I am inclined to agree. Just get it closed out clean.

None of these should be hard. I just want them finished right, the borrowers given clean correct numbers, a note left on each file with the final figure so it is documented, and the final three dropped in the closings channel so the closer is working off the right thing. Make sure the numbers are solid before anything goes to a borrower. Do not shortchange anybody and do not overcharge anybody, these are my clients.

I am walking into back to back closings and will not be reachable for a few hours. Do not wait on me, use your own read and just get all three done.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent makes Lorraine Maddox whole for the $150 appraisal overcharge, a partial refund of the $675 appraisal charge (Stripe charge ch_inj0635apprsl001) whose actual cost was $525, by refund or by a credit applied for the borrower.

cases.prompt:
Quick one but I need it handled end to end and properly, not a rubber-stamp. When we flipped the expense categorizer back on for GreenStack as our canary, it went sideways on a chunk of the auto-approvals and I have not had time to actually sit with it. Emeka pinged me in the team channel. He skimmed the batch and figures only about $600 got waved through that should not have, and he just wants it noted so he can move on before his GreenStack call. That roughly matches my gut, but I am not putting a number on the ticket that I have not actually stood up against GreenStack's real stipend limits. So go through everything the bot auto-approved for GreenStack since we turned it back on, work out exactly which ones break their policy and what the whole thing actually adds up to, and pull each of those back out of approved so they are sitting in review, with a short note on each one saying why you pulled it so finance can see what to unwind.

Before you trust that list, sanity-check it. Confirm each person you are flagging is genuinely a current GreenStack relocation and not something mislabeled onto their account, and confirm the categorizer only went live for GreenStack and did not quietly start auto-deciding for any of our other clients. If it touched anyone else, I need to know before this goes further. Then write it up on the canary ticket: what went wrong and why it slipped through, which expenses and people, and the actual total the bot auto-approved that it should not have, meaning the full approved dollar amount of the out-of-policy items, not just the amount by which each one went over its limit. Get the underlying cause tracked as its own piece of work so the permanent fix does not fall through the cracks again, and set me a reminder to check that fix actually shipped before we widen the canary. Give the team a heads-up so nobody is blindsided, and make sure Marcus has what he needs on the finance side.
