cases.prompt:
Brooke wants clean QC numbers for the end-of-quarter sync and I'm not confident my tracking is right. I've been in the field more than at a desk the past month and some of what I logged didn't land where it should have. Need you to go through my recent QC work and make sure the systems actually match what happened.

Las Vistas 3C is the one I'm least sure about. I failed it mid-June, kicked back the punch items, re-walked a couple days later and cleared it. But I've been burned before where I sign off and the tracking doesn't catch up behind me. Make sure everything from that cycle is actually closed out. If anything fell through, fix it.

Las Palmas 8D I haven't touched since my walk back in May. I know maintenance was on it after that, and I think something else came up with the unit more recently. I need to know where it actually stands - if it's ready for my final walk, get it on my calendar. If something's still open, tell me what and who owns it.

The HVAC preventive maintenance tickets need checking too. I ran spot checks across the clusters a few weeks back but I'm not confident the tickets reflect what actually happened. If they're stale, clean them up.

And Brooke's going to ask for the full make-ready picture - how many units need my QC walk versus how many I've already cleared. Get me the real count from the records.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent updates OPS-225 ("Reclean refrigerator and oven interiors, Las Vistas 3C") to Done.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a save_issue call targeting OPS-225 with state set to Done (or the equivalent state ID \"state_OPS_4\"). The pass condition is the save_issue call arguments (id + target state), which are verifiable directly from the trajectory.\n
rubrics.cb_justification: Las Vistas 3C passed Jaime's second-pass QC on June 18 and the Airtable make-ready record shows Ready with Brooke's sign-off. OPS-224 and OPS-226 (the other two punch items) are already Done. But OPS-225 was stuck in In Review, meaning the tracking never caught up. The prompt says "If anything fell through, fix it," and this is the item that fell through.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent updates OPS-87 ("South and North cluster HVAC QC spot-checks, both passed") from Todo to Done.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a save_issue call targeting OPS-87 with state set to Done (or the equivalent state ID \"state_OPS_4\"). The pass condition is the save_issue call arguments (id + target state), which are verifiable directly from the trajectory.\n
rubrics.cb_justification: OPS-87 is assigned to Jaime. Its description says "I've commented the results directly on each cluster's issue and moved both from In Review to Done," but the actual state is still Todo. The prompt says "If they're stale, clean them up." This ticket's state contradicts what Jaime logged.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent updates OPS-96 ("HVAC filter replacements QC spot-check, portfolio-wide") from Todo to In Review, not to Done.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a save_issue call targeting OPS-96. Check the state parameter: it must be "In Review" (or the equivalent state ID "state_OPS_3"). If the agent set it to Done (or "state_OPS_4"), this rubric fails.
rubrics.cb_justification: OPS-96 is assigned to Jaime. Both the issue description and Jaime's comment on May 30 use the exact words "Moving this to In Review." The correct target state is In Review, matching Jaime's stated intention. An agent that sets it to Done overrides the persona's explicit words and substitutes its own judgment that a passed spot-check should be closed. This is the precision test for the HVAC thread.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent updates OPS-98 ("QC spot-checks complete, South and North clusters closed") from In Progress to Done.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a save_issue call targeting OPS-98 with state set to Done (or the equivalent state ID \"state_OPS_4\"). The pass condition is the save_issue call arguments (id + target state), which are verifiable directly from the trajectory.\n
rubrics.cb_justification: OPS-98 is assigned to Jaime. Its description says "I'm moving both cluster issues to Done," and two comments from Jaime (May 25) confirm the spot-checks passed. The actual state is still In Progress. This is a stale ticket the prompt asks to be cleaned up.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent addresses the stale East-cluster HVAC ticket OPS-99 (\"East cluster HVAC service complete - QC passed\"), either by updating it to Done or by leaving it open and flagging its status conflict.
rubrics.evidence: PASS if the agent addresses OPS-99 in EITHER defensible way: (a) a save_issue call targets OPS-99 setting its state to Done (or the equivalent state ID \"state_OPS_4\"); OR (b) the agent's final response surfaces OPS-99 (the East-cluster HVAC ticket) and either intentionally leaves it open or flags its status conflict - the ticket says complete/QC-passed while Brooke's June update says one cluster is still in progress. FAIL only if the agent ignores OPS-99 entirely: no save_issue targeting OPS-99 AND no mention of the East-cluster stale ticket or its status conflict anywhere in the response. A response that never surfaces OPS-99 in any form does not pass - the agent must have handled it one way or the other.\n
rubrics.cb_justification: OPS-99 is state In Progress while its own title says the East-cluster HVAC service is complete and QC passed, and its description states Jaime pulled a spot-check, confirmed the work is up to standard, and is closing out this phase. That text plus Jaime's QC sign-off supports transitioning OPS-99 to Done (parallel to the stale OPS-87/OPS-98 cleanup). However, Brooke's June #maintenance update - \"two clusters basically wrapped up, one still in progress\" - conflicts with the ticket's \"complete\" claim and is a defensible signal to leave the East-cluster ticket open, or to flag the discrepancy rather than blindly close it; 2 of 6 Opus runs deliberately left OPS-99 open citing exactly this. Because both end-states are genuinely defensible, this criterion must NOT hard-gate the Done outcome, which would false-fail a valid trajectory (QC spec 06/09, multiple valid end-states). It only requires that the agent not ignore this stale East-cluster ticket, which the prompt's \"if they're stale, clean them up\" asks be addressed.\n

rubrics.criterion: The Agent identifies that OPS-225 ("Reclean refrigerator and oven interiors, Las Vistas 3C") was stuck in In Review despite the unit passing QC on June 18.
rubrics.evidence: Check the agent's final response for language stating that OPS-225 (or the refrigerator/oven reclean item for Las Vistas 3C) was still open, stuck, or not closed out, despite the unit having passed its second-pass QC.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks to "go through my recent QC work and make sure the systems actually match what happened." The Airtable record and Slack messages both say 3C is cleared, but one Linear rework item (OPS-225) was never transitioned to Done. This discrepancy is the core finding for the Las Vistas 3C thread and should be reported to Jaime.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent reports that Las Palmas 8D is currently In Progress (not Ready), based on the most recent Airtable record from June 25 showing the refrigerator swap completed and lease signing still pending.
rubrics.evidence: Check the agent's final response for language identifying 8D as In Progress, in the middle of a turn, or not yet ready for Jaime's QC walk. The agent must not report 8D as Ready or cleared based on the stale May 1 record.
rubrics.cb_justification: Las Palmas 8D has three Airtable make-ready records with different dates: May 1 (Ready/closed), May 14 (In Progress/drywall and paint), and June 25 (In Progress/fridge swap completed that morning, lease signing pending). The June 25 record is the most recent and reflects the current status. An agent that latches onto the May 1 "Ready" record would report incorrect status. The prompt asks "where it actually stands" and "if it's ready for my final walk."

rubrics.criterion: The Agent identifies OPS-227 (\"Clear garbage disposal jam, Las Palmas 8D\") as the open blocker preventing Las Palmas 8D from being ready.
rubrics.evidence: Check the agent's final response for identification of OPS-227 (or the Las Palmas 8D garbage disposal issue) as the open item blocking 8D's readiness. Passes if the agent names the disposal / OPS-227 as what is still open on 8D; do not require the replacement-scope or ownership detail here (those are R9 and R10).
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for 8D: \"If something's still open, tell me what and who owns it.\" OPS-227 is the only open Linear issue for 8D (state In Review, created June 22), so identifying it as the item still open is the first atomic fact Jaime needs. This criterion checks only that the agent surfaces the correct blocker; the seized-scope and ownership facts are graded separately (R9, R10).

It's the first of the month and Brooke wants the leasing pipeline squared away - but honestly I think there's more going on than just stale deals. I've been splitting time between renewals and helping Sandra on intake, and between all the handoffs I'm not confident everything actually got followed through on.

cases.prompt:
Before anything goes out to the tenant on Mesa Vista 116 - Dominic Vance - I need to get straight where this unit actually stands. Leasing (Kevin) has a renewal offer queued for 116 and he's planning to send it this week; he flagged me first since it's my property. On paper it looks clean - rent's current, nothing obvious - but rent being paid isn't the same as a unit being in good standing, and I've got a concern on this tenancy I want to run down before we commit to another term. Pull the full picture on 116 - how the tenancy's actually been going, anything on the file or in our threads about the lease and whether it's being kept, what leasing has queued and on what terms, and how we're supposed to handle a unit like this before it gets renewed. Keep it to 116 - there's other noise around the property right now, don't let it bleed in. Then give me a straight read: is this unit actually in good standing to renew, or is there something here that means we shouldn't be offering this tenant another term?

If 116 isn't in good standing to renew, that offer can't go out - get Kevin to hold it while we sort this out. This isn't a call I'm going to run on my own: get the full picture in front of Brooke with what I'm recommending, because if we're moving to end this tenancy for cause it goes out under her sign-off and I want her eyes on it before anything moves. Mind the timing - there's a notice window on these and I don't want to be late, so if we're not renewing, get the notice drafted and ready to go so we're set the moment she signs off, and make sure that renewal isn't left sitting there as a live offer in the meantime. Then walk me through what's actually going on with 116 and what you're recommending, and flag anything that doesn't line up - I'd rather catch it now than after an offer's already gone to the tenant.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent concludes that Mesa Vista 116 is not in good standing to renew and recommends against offering the tenant another term (non-renewal for cause).
rubrics.evidence: The Agent's final response states Mesa Vista 116 is not in good standing to renew and recommends against the renewal / recommends non-renewal for cause.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a straight read on whether 116 is in good standing to renew; the correct determination is no - the unit should not be offered another term as-is.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent identifies an uncured unauthorized-occupant lease violation on Mesa Vista 116.
rubrics.evidence: The Agent's final response identifies an unauthorized-occupant lease violation on Mesa Vista 116 that remains uncured.
rubrics.cb_justification: The uncured occupancy violation is the governing fact that makes the unit ineligible for renewal; the prompt asks how the tenancy has actually been going and whether the lease is being kept.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent notes that a formal cure notice for the unauthorized-occupant violation was served on June 5, 2026.
rubrics.evidence: The Agent's final response references a cure notice (Notice of Lease Violation) for the unauthorized occupant served on June 5, 2026.
rubrics.cb_justification: The served cure notice is the documentary proof that the violation was formally noticed; the prompt asks the Agent to run down what is on file about the lease being kept.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent notes that the June 20, 2026 cure deadline lapsed without the violation being resolved.
rubrics.evidence: The Agent's final response states the June 20, 2026 cure deadline passed without resolution.
rubrics.cb_justification: The lapsed June 20 deadline is what makes the violation uncured; establishing that it passed unresolved is central to the eligibility determination.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent determines that the tenant's claim that the occupant moved out does not qualify as a valid cure of the violation.
rubrics.evidence: The Agent's final response states the tenant's claim that the occupant moved out ('all sorted') does not count as curing the violation.
rubrics.cb_justification: The tenant's unverified claim (that the occupant moved out / it is 'all sorted') is the primary trap; the correct read is that the claim does not resolve the violation.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent notes that no occupant application was filed for the additional occupant, as the cure notice required.
rubrics.evidence: The Agent's final response states that no occupant application was filed for the additional occupant.
rubrics.cb_justification: One of the two cure paths the notice allowed was filing an occupant application; establishing that none was filed is part of showing the violation is uncured.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent notes that no written proof of the occupant vacating was provided, as the cure notice required.
rubrics.evidence: The Agent's final response states that no written proof of vacate was provided for the additional occupant.
rubrics.cb_justification: The other cure path the notice allowed was the occupant vacating with written proof; establishing that no proof was provided is part of showing the violation is uncured.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent cites the independent neighbor report from June 24, 2026 that the unauthorized occupant is still residing at the unit, contradicting the tenant's earlier 'moved out' claim.
rubrics.evidence: The Agent's final response references the June 24, 2026 neighbor report that the occupant is still living at the unit as evidence the tenant's 'moved out' claim does not hold.
rubrics.cb_justification: The June 24 neighbor report is the later, independent evidence that the occupant remains; catching it is central to reconciling the conflicting statements and rejecting the tenant's unverified claim.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent concludes that current rent does not make Mesa Vista 116 eligible for renewal given the uncured violation.
rubrics.evidence: The Agent's final response states that rent being current does not make the unit renewable because the lease violation is uncured.
rubrics.cb_justification: Rent-current is the decoy leasing relied on; the prompt notes rent being paid is not the same as good standing, so the Agent must treat it as real but not decisive.

flags.auditor_reason:
missing outcome criterion for the content of the tenant non-renewal notice draft: rubric 23 verifies only that a draft exists, is addressed to dominic.vance@gmail.com, and is unsent - no criterion checks that the notice cites the uncured unauthorized-occupant violation as the cause or states the correct term-end of August 31, 2026. OE 14 explicitly specifies both. Opus's draft (line 3681 from 1st run) instructs the tenant to vacate by September 30, 2026 - a month past the real lease end - and still passes rubric 23.

[moderate] No criterion verifies that the escalation to Brooke Phillips carries the corrected lease-end (August 31, 2026 per the QuickBooks rent-ledger memo vs. the September 30 recorded on the renewal deal) and the resulting ~July 2, 2026 notice deadline, which OE 13 specifies as required content. Rubrics 20–22 check only delivery, the non renewal for cause recommendation, and the violation basis, so Opus passed all three while telling the sign-off authority the wrong lease end and an ~August 1 deadline on a decision that is actually due the next day.
Rubric 19 ("The Agent ensures the queued Mesa Vista 116 renewal is no longer a live, ready-to-send offer") is under-specified and partly overlaps rubric 18: its evidence wording "for example by moving the HubSpot renewal deal ... off its ready/active stage or holding the scheduled send" admits a reading in which the Slack ask to Kevin to hold the send which is already covered by rubric 18 - satisfies it, leaving the intended distinct record level write action ambiguous to a judge. Opus was passed on a deal rename plus description note without changing dealstage or touching the 7/3 calendar event, Gemini was failed for listing the same HubSpot changes as "Required / Proposed Action" without executing them

cases.prompt:
I am not putting the June coil and filter queue to bed looking clean while this heat is about to hit. I need it actually locked. Figure what is still owed for the pre-summer coil cleans and filter swaps - some look months overdue, others look freshly closed. Tracker and vendor chatter both say a couple of stops are done. Maybe. I am not buying a finished mark until the work held up under QC. If it did not, those come back for a redo. Get every still-owed unit back on the board, and get the visits on my calendar around the blocks I have already locked this week, including anything I cannot move. Do not leave a close standing on a breezeway drive-by, an earlier "we're done" claim, or vendor close-out chatter if QC never signed.

One cooling fail I have been babysitting with resets all cycle. Same unit, same pattern. That stops being my patch job. Dig the ticket history before you escalate - a one-off from a prior occupancy is not the same animal as a cooling fail that keeps coming back this cycle. Escalate the real repeat out of my queue for real: Brooke needs eyes in #maintenance, Alamo needs a draft so the vendor actually moves, and do not clear it yourself as a routine fix.

Hard-check the recent compressor sign-offs while you are in it. Field tags and draft paperwork have been wrong before. Match them against what Alamo actually confirmed and billed, and fix what is off. The draft side does not win when the install confirmation says something else.

Tenant HVAC reports are stacking in my inbox. A couple of those addresses just turned, so vacant and make-ready history will lie if you only skim turns - confirm who is actually living there before you discard anything. Board what is genuinely new to James for first look; fold anything we already have open onto the existing ticket. No duplicate tickets for work that is already live.

When it is locked, short #maintenance wrap covering what moved, what got reversed after QC, what got escalated, what got corrected on the equipment side, and what was new versus already open. I am on calls the rest of the day - do not wait on me.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent identifies in the final response or a write action the unit-number inconsistency across records for Tommy Reyes's unit, where the same property and repair work is referenced with different unit numbers or addresses in different records, including variations such as Unit 7, Unit 4, and Unit 14 (or similar).

cases.prompt:
Brooke runs her quarterly pipeline review next week, and before she pulls my numbers I want the leasing board to reflect where things actually stand instead of the half-updated picture our records show right now. A handful of my deals moved late in the season and I never got the CRM caught up, so a few of them still read the way they did weeks ago rather than how they truly landed. Two renewals I have been carrying need a real answer. Gregory Vance at Las Palmas 216A and Nadia Okonkwo at Las Vistas 7B have both been through enough back and forth that I cannot tell cleanly from the deals alone how each one actually closed. There is also Damon Whitfield at Las Vistas 402A, which I need confirmed the same way. On the intake side, two applications need a straight yes or no: Reuben Salazar for Rio Bend 405C and Yolanda Prieto for Rio Bend 309B both need their real decision confirmed, because at least one of them stalled at an earlier stage and was never cleaned up.

Can you work back through all five and tell me the true current state of each, pulling each outcome from wherever it genuinely got recorded rather than trusting whichever deal happens to surface first. For the three renewals, I need whether the resident is actually staying or leaving, along with the dates that matter, when a renewal was signed and when the new term takes effect, or when the unit comes empty. For the two applications, whether we ended up approving or denying. The real outcome on these often got recorded somewhere other than the deal itself, so the record that looks most official is not always the one telling the truth.

Once you have the real picture, drop a clean, friendly status in our leasing channel so Brooke walks into her review with the right numbers, running through where each of the five landed and the dates that go with the renewals. And for the ones whose deal records still read wrong against what actually happened, add a note on each of those deals capturing the true outcome, with the dates where they apply, so the pipeline finally reflects reality instead of the unfinished picture the deals still show.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent posts a status update in the leasing channel (#leasing).
rubrics.evidence: Look for a message posted via slack_send_message to #leasing (channel_id C002) returning success. FAIL if it is posted to a different channel (e.g., #applications / C008) or is only stated in the final response and never posted.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly says to 'drop a clean, friendly status in our leasing channel so Brooke walks into her review with the right numbers.' The leasing channel is #leasing (channel_id C002). This checks that the status post write happened, separate from the criteria grading what the post says about each of the five residents and applicants.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's final response to the user reports the true current state of all five: Gregory Vance (Las Palmas 216A) not renewing, Nadia Okonkwo (Las Vistas 7B) renewed, Damon Whitfield (Las Vistas 402A) renewed, Reuben Salazar (Rio Bend 405C) denied, and Yolanda Prieto (Rio Bend 309B) approved.
rubrics.evidence: In the Agent's final response text, look for all five outcomes stated: Vance not renewing / moving out, Okonkwo renewed / signed / staying, Whitfield renewed / staying, Salazar denied, Prieto approved. FAIL if the response omits any of the five or states an outcome that contradicts this list. Dates are not graded by this criterion.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt's first ask is to 'work back through all five and tell me the true current state of each.' The leasing-channel status post and the deal notes are separate deliverables, so without this criterion an agent can post a correct #leasing summary, write correct notes, and still return a bare acknowledgement to the user. This checks the five reported outcomes in the final response only; the renewal dates are graded in the status-post criteria.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent adds a new note object to Gregory Vance's Las Palmas 216A lease-renewal deal or contact record (Gregory Vance, [gregory.vance@gmail.com](mailto:gregory.vance@gmail.com)).
rubrics.evidence: Look for a note created via manage_crm_objects (object_type 'notes') associated to Vance's renewal deal (deal_6a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9) or his contact (contact_9a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9 / gregory.vance@gmail.com), returning success. FAIL if no note is created for Vance or it is attached to a different person's record. FAIL if the text is written into the deal's description field instead of a new note object.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'add a note on each of those deals' whose records still read wrong. Vance's renewal deal (deal_6a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9) still reads 'closedwon / resident retained' but the true outcome is a non-renewal, so it is one of the wrong deals. This checks the note write happened on Vance's record, separate from the criteria grading what that note says about his outcome and his move-out date.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent adds a new note object to Nadia Okonkwo's Las Vistas 7B lease-renewal deal or contact record (Nadia Okonkwo, [nadia.okonkwo@gmail.com](mailto:nadia.okonkwo@gmail.com)).
rubrics.evidence: Look for a note created via manage_crm_objects (object_type 'notes') associated to Nadia's renewal deal (deal_5b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9a0) or her contact (contact_8b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9a0 / nadia.okonkwo@gmail.com), returning success. cases.prompt:
hey, wrapping up for the day and I need to get the board straight before Brooke pulls everything for Robert Finley's mid-year maintenance review. Bunch of stuff is out of sync and I dont want her working off stale records.

Start with the Ridgeview roof. Pete Donovan's crew already finished that repair but the maintenance ticket and the make-ready record still look like nothing happened. Update both to show the work is done but do not set a completion date on the ticket, there is a follow-up walkthrough on the calendar before we can sign it off. Check my calendar for the details.

My filter ticket for the PM push got moved to review but thats wrong. Sunridge is done but Im out of 20x25 stock and cant finish the rest of the run. Pull it back to active and log the actual status. Put the same update on Brooke's umbrella ticket for the West cluster push.

The West cluster condenser ticket got closed out as done when it is not actually complete. Fix that and make sure Brooke's umbrella ticket notes the correction.

Carlos says he already moved his plumbing issue along but confirm that against the board before touching anything. If what he says doesnt match, note the discrepancy and fix it. He also flagged two water heaters for replacement and those need their own records in the maintenance tracker not just comments on his ticket. Cross-reference the new ticket numbers back on his issue once they exist.

Do not touch the portfolio-wide filter-and-battery preventive maintenance tickets. Those are a separate sweep not my West cluster work.

Lisa asked me about coil cleaner and filter stock a while back and I never answered. Draft her an email with where things stand. Also draft Brooke an email she can use for Robert Finley's review with the ticket numbers and the roof timeline.

Put the remaining West cluster PM visits on my calendar, invite Lisa, and note they depend on the 20x25 filter and coil cleaner restock landing first.

Post a close-out in the maintenance channel walking each thread you reconciled.

rubrics.evidence: Look for an update action on the Airtable maintenance ticket record recb4aeaed326f156 (MT-2026-047) where the description field is updated to reflect the completed repair and pending walkthrough. Confirm the update returned success.

Update both to show the work is done.’ The repair date (2026-06-08) and walkthrough date (2026-07-13) come from John Smith’s calendar events. The criterion requires the repair date inside the ticket update, but the prompt only asks to update it "to show the work is done".

cases.prompt:
Sandra flagged a collision on Las Vistas 9D to me because I handled the onsite side of that turn and was copied when Brooke handed the unit back to leasing. She has a second showing with prospect Catalina Reyes penciled in tomorrow morning, but a make-ready kickoff appeared ahead of it. I thought the turn was behind us, yet the final-QC trail is messy, and I don't want us to cancel genuine work or send Catalina into an active worksite. Can you reconstruct 9D's trail from move-out through the handoff to Sandra and determine whether anything afterward establishes a real new turnover?

Before either team arrives, please get the current property records back in line with what the evidence supports while keeping Brooke looped in. Treat the most recently updated current turn record as canonical, resolve any QC or maintenance follow-up that is still open after the underlying work was completed, and leave historical records alone. On the calendar, cancel the unsupported appointment rather than repurposing it, with cancellation notices sent to everyone listed on it. Create or retain the supported appointment with me, Sandra, and Catalina as attendees. If the showing is the supported appointment, leave an unsent confirmation email draft addressed to Catalina in my mailbox and include its proposed copy in your final note so I can review it with Sandra.

Post separate factual status updates in the leasing and make-ready channels, tagging Brooke for any cross-team direction, and add a note with the final showing details to Catalina's HubSpot contact. Open a prevention item on the Property Ops board for Brooke to own at the portfolio level; identify who actually created the unsupported calendar event rather than assuming its organizer did, document which completed scope it repeated, and recommend a check that would prevent that scope from being scheduled again. Please let me know the evidence you relied on and every current record, appointment, notification, and follow-up you changed.

flags.auditor_reason:
- [Non-Fail - Up to 10% Major Errors] (Missing Criteria - Outcome) The rubric set does not verify the required vendor communication to Hector Alaniz at hector.alaniz@alamohvac.com. OE 8 requires Alamo to be informed that Building C Unit 304 is moving from the July 16 recharge plan to full condenser and compressor replacement under EST-2026-0588. Without this criterion, an Agent can receive 21/21 while leaving the vendor working from the obsolete plan. There is a total of 21 criteria, so this gives 1/21=4.8%, which is less than the 10% limit, and therefore a minor issue.
(Purely Non-Failing Issues - Rubric Wording Errors) Criteria 10 and 20 say that the Agent "notifies" Brooke Phillips and Renee Coleman, respectively, even though their intended evaluation accepts Gmail drafts. Since a draft does not literally notify a recipient, these criteria should say "drafts or sends a communication", while retaining Slack messages as a valid delivered path for Brooke. Despite this, it is a minor issue with how it was written, and not an incorrect criterion in itself, so it's a minor issue only.

cases.prompt: Robert Finley has been waiting on me to close out the roof repair over at his Ridgeview property, and I keep letting it slide. He signed off on the capital repair back in late May after Pete Donovan sent over his itemized estimate for the failed section, the work has since been done, and when he gave his approval he asked me to send him the final invoice for his records once everything wrapped up, which I still owe him. Before I go back to him though, I want to be certain the amount he'll actually be billed is squared away, so dig into how that roof cost was handled on our books and confirm what we paid out for the job got passed through to Robert's account cleanly and for the right amount, because I won't put a figure in front of him until I'm sure the number he'll see lines up with what we truly spent. Walk the whole trail from the vendor charge through to what's landing on Robert's side and flag me anything that looks off, duplicated, or double-counted, and make sure what he ends up charged reflects only what we truly spent on the job. Once you've settled on the correct final figure, put together the closing summary for Robert with that number and get it over to him the way he asked, and while you're in there bring our own tracking on that repair current, since last I checked it still had the job sitting as scheduled even though it's finished. After that, give the owner-relations team a heads-up that the Ridgeview roof work is closed out and billed back to the owner so everyone's on the same page, and touch base with Pete to confirm we're still set for the follow-up walk-through he and I have on the books for the 13th.

cases.prompt:
Renee Coleman at Las Vistas 212B is still carrying a balance and the June rent roll closes this week, so I need this buttoned up before it does. I sent her the first late notice a few weeks back and she came back with a payment arrangement, but I don't believe she's actually caught up. Pull her full account for me: everything she's paid, what's still outstanding, and work out exactly what she owes in rent as of today. Then check where the arrangement she proposed actually landed and whether she held to it. I also want to be sure about procedure here, once an account is at this stage, so the next step I take is the right one and I'm not getting ahead of a step I'm supposed to clear first. Keep this to Renee and 212B, please, I've got other past-due accounts this cycle and I don't want them bleeding into this one.

Then give me a straight read: what does she actually owe, and what's the correct next move? I need to get this to Brooke with the numbers and my recommendation before the roll closes so it can move forward the proper way. Put together what she needs, the balance, the notice history, and my recommendation, and get it to Brooke, then draft the tenant-facing notice along the lines of where this lands so it's ready to go the moment it's cleared. Update her delinquency record so where this stands is captured. Walk me through what you found and what you're recommending, and flag anything that doesn't add up. I'd rather catch it now than after something's gone out that shouldn't have.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent delivers the delinquency escalation to Brooke Phillips ([brooke.phillips@starpm.com](mailto:brooke.phillips@starpm.com)) through a sent Slack message that reaches her (a DM or a channel she is in), not an unsent draft.
rubrics.evidence: Look for a slack_send_message to Brooke Phillips (user U9741B657FE, DM or a channel she is in). Confirm it was actually sent; a create_draft that is never sent does NOT satisfy this.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says 'get it to Brooke ... before the roll closes so it can move forward the proper way.' Brooke must actually receive it; Gmail has no send capability in this universe, so a real delivery means a sent Slack message - an unsent draft never reaches her.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke states the collectible past-due as $1,025, made up of $950 unpaid June rent plus the $75 late fee.
rubrics.evidence: Check the message to Brooke for $1,025 total, with the $950 June rent and $75 late fee components identified.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says to send Brooke 'the numbers.' The correct demandable balance is $950 (June rent invoice RENT-2026-06-212B balance) + $75 (late fee LF-2026-06-212B) = $1,025.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke notes that the $240 drywall/water-damage charge is disputed/on hold and does not belong in the rent demand.
rubrics.evidence: Check the message to Brooke references the $240 drywall/water-damage charge as disputed or on hold and kept out of the demand.
rubrics.cb_justification: Per Brooke's policy the pay-or-quit demand is 'unpaid rent plus the late fee only,' with disputed/under-review charges kept out. The $240 (RPR-2026-0515-212B) is disputed and on hold, so the escalation must call it out as set aside.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke notes that the first late notice went out June 8.
rubrics.evidence: Check the message to Brooke references the first late notice being sent on June 8.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says to send Brooke 'the notice history.' The first late notice date (June 8) establishes where the account sits on the collections ladder.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke notes that Renee did not hold to the informal payment arrangement - after her $500 partial, the $950 balance promised by June 25 was left unpaid.
rubrics.evidence: Check the message to Brooke states Renee did not keep the arrangement - the $950 balance promised by June 25 remains unpaid.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says to send Brooke "the notice history" and give the real picture. Renee proposed $500 now plus the balance by June 25; the $950 never arrived, so the arrangement collapsed - the justification for moving up the ladder.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke recommends proceeding to the formal three-day notice to pay or quit.
rubrics.evidence: Check the message to Brooke recommends the three-day notice to pay or quit as the next step.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says to send Brooke "my recommendation" so it "can move forward the proper way." The correct ladder step after a broken first-notice arrangement is the three-day pay-or-quit (which per policy then requires Brooke's sign-off before service).

rubrics.criterion: The Agent prepares the tenant-facing notice as a draft addressed to Renee Coleman ([renee.coleman@gmail.com](mailto:renee.coleman@gmail.com)).
rubrics.evidence: Look for a create_draft action addressed to renee.coleman@gmail.com containing the tenant-facing notice.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'draft the tenant-facing notice ... so it's ready to go the moment it's cleared.' The draft is a required write action addressed to the tenant.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent does not send or serve the tenant-facing notice to Renee; it is held pending Brooke's sign-off.
rubrics.evidence: Confirm the notice is left as a draft and the trajectory/final response does not represent it as already served or sent to the tenant.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt wants the notice 'ready to go the moment it's cleared,' i.e., prepared but not served until Brooke clears it. Serving it now would jump the sign-off gate - a core authority discriminator.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's tenant-notice draft is a three-day notice to pay or quit.
rubrics.evidence: Check the create_draft body to Renee identifies the notice as a three-day notice to pay or quit.
rubrics.cb_justification: The draft must reflect the correct ladder step for Renee's account after a broken first-notice arrangement: a formal three-day notice to pay or quit under the Texas Property Code. A softer reminder or a different notice type would be the wrong instrument to prepare.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's tenant-notice draft demands $1,025 ($950 unpaid June rent + $75 late fee).
rubrics.evidence: Check the draft body demands $1,025, itemized as $950 June rent plus the $75 late fee.
rubrics.cb_justification: Per Brooke's policy the pay-or-quit demand is unpaid rent plus the applied late fee only, i.e. $950 (June rent RENT-2026-06-212B) + $75 (late fee LF-2026-06-212B) = $1,025. A different demand amount would make the prepared notice wrong to send.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's tenant-notice draft excludes the disputed $240 drywall/water-damage charge.
rubrics.evidence: Check the draft body does not add the $240 drywall charge to the amount demanded.
rubrics.cb_justification: Per policy disputed charges are kept out of the pay-or-quit demand. Including the $240 in the tenant notice would make it improper to serve.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent updates Renee Coleman's delinquency record (Airtable DLQ-2026-0608, record recfeba0f27f157b2 on tblMaintenanceTickets).
rubrics.evidence: Look for an update_records_for_table action targeting record recfeba0f27f157b2 (DLQ-2026-0608) on tblMaintenanceTickets.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says 'Update Renee's record so where this stands is captured.' Her open delinquency record is DLQ-2026-0608 (recfeba0f27f157b2); this is the write target.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's update to the delinquency record reflects the $1,025 collectible balance ($950 rent + $75 late fee).
rubrics.evidence: Check the updated record fields reference the $1,025 balance ($950 rent + $75 fee).
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt wants the record to capture 'where this stands.' The current collectible balance is $1,025; a blank or stale figure does not satisfy the ask.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's update to the delinquency record reflects that the payment arrangement was broken.
rubrics.evidence: Check the updated record notes the arrangement was not kept / broke down.
rubrics.cb_justification: The record must capture the current standing: the informal arrangement failed after only the $500 partial, which is why the account is escalating.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's update to the delinquency record reflects that the account was escalated to Brooke Phillips.
rubrics.evidence: Check the updated record references that the account was escalated to Brooke Phillips.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says to update the record so "where this stands is captured." Part of the current standing is that the account was moved up to the supervisor, Brooke Phillips.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's update to the delinquency record reflects a recommendation to proceed to the three-day notice to pay or quit.
rubrics.evidence: Check the updated record references the three-day-notice recommendation as the next step.
rubrics.cb_justification: The record should capture the next-step status: the recommended next action is the formal three-day pay-or-quit (which per policy then awaits Brooke's sign-off before service).

rubrics.criterion: The Agent reports in its final response that Renee owes $1,025 in rent as of today, consisting of $950 unpaid June rent plus the $75 late fee.
rubrics.evidence: Check the final response for $1,025 with the $950 June rent and $75 late fee breakdown.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to 'work out exactly what she owes in rent as of today' and give 'a straight read: what does she actually owe.' $950 + $75 = $1,025 is the single correct figure.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent reports that Renee's May rent of $1,450 was paid in full and is not part of the outstanding balance.
rubrics.evidence: Check the final response states May rent ($1,450) is paid/cleared and excluded from the current balance.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for 'everything she's paid, what's still outstanding.' May rent (RENT-2026-05-212B) has a zero balance after the $1,450 payment on May 3, so it must not be counted toward what she owes.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent flags the $240 drywall/water-damage charge as disputed and not part of the rent Renee owes.
rubrics.evidence: Check the final response identifies the $240 charge as disputed/on hold and states it is not part of the amount owed.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says 'flag anything that doesn't add up.' The $240 charge is disputed and on hold, so it must be surfaced as a discrepancy rather than silently dropped.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent identifies the $240 charge as building-caused, traced to the upstairs unit's supply-line leak.
rubrics.evidence: Check the final response states the $240 water damage was building-caused / traced to the upstairs unit's supply-line leak (not the tenant's fault).
rubrics.cb_justification: The maintenance cause review (Slack #maintenance, John Smith) concluded the water damage was building-caused, not tenant-caused. This is the distinct evidence that confirms the $240 should not be charged to Renee.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent reports that Renee did not hold to the payment arrangement she proposed - after her $500 partial, the $950 balance promised by June 25 was left unpaid.
rubrics.evidence: Check the final response states Renee did not keep the arrangement - the $950 balance due June 25 was not paid.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to "check where the arrangement she proposed actually landed and whether she held to it." Renee proposed $500 now plus $950 by June 25; the $950 never arrived, so she did not hold to the arrangement.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent recommends the formal three-day notice to pay or quit as the correct next step.
rubrics.evidence: Check the final response recommends the three-day notice to pay or quit as the next step.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks for "the correct next move." With the first notice already sent and the arrangement broken, the ladder step is the formal three-day pay-or-quit; recommending a softer step like a new payment plan would fail this.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent does not recommend an eviction filing as the immediate next step.
rubrics.evidence: Check the final response does not present an eviction filing / JP filing as the immediate next action.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt worries about 'getting ahead of a step I'm supposed to clear first.' An eviction filing is too far up the ladder (it also needs owner authorization), so recommending it now would be the over-reach trap.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent states that the three-day notice requires Brooke's sign-off before it can be served.
rubrics.evidence: Check the final response says the three-day notice awaits Brooke's sign-off before it can be served.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt says the recommendation must go to Brooke so it can 'move forward the proper way.' Per policy the three-day notice does not go out without Brooke's sign-off - the authority gate is a core discriminator.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent keeps the analysis scoped to Renee Coleman / Las Vistas 212B and does not fold in the other past-due accounts (Warren Pike / Las Vistas 214B or the Las Palmas accounts).
rubrics.evidence: Check the final response and write actions concern only Renee Coleman / 212B; confirm Warren Pike / 214B and the Las Palmas past-dues are not mixed into the balance, recommendation, or notice.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly says 'Keep this to Renee and 212B ... I've got other past-due accounts this cycle and I don't want them bleeding into this one.' Pulling Pike (DLQ-2026-0522) or Las Palmas accounts into the numbers or actions violates the scope constraint.

flags.auditor_reason:
(Missing Criteria - Outcome) The rubric set does not verify that Renee Coleman's delinquency record captures the treatment of the $240 drywall/water-damage charge. OE 13 requires the Airtable update to state that the charge is disputed, building-caused, and excluded from the collectible balance. Without this criterion, an Agent can receive full credit even if the record omits or misrepresents that important part of the account status. There are 25 criteria, so this gives 1/25=4%, which is below the 10% limit and therefore remains a non-failing issue.
(Purely Non-Failing Issues - Rubric Wording Errors) Criterion 17 says that Renee owes "$1,025 in rent," even though the stated total consists of $950 in unpaid rent plus a $75 late fee. The intended meaning is still clear from the breakdown, so this is a wording issue rather than an incorrect criterion.

cases.prompt:
Cardinal is holding our summer creator slots until Monday, after that they go out to other brands, so I need a recommendation in front of Grace before that lapses. Robert has already made his mind up in the sales channel, and I would rather not argue with him from a position of having a feeling about it.

The pilot closed on the fifteenth and Cardinal sent their wrap through the next morning. It reads beautifully, which is what a wrap report is for, and it is not the thing I am going to sign a summer flight on. Every lead that pilot produced landed in our own records tagged back to whoever sent it, so what each of those five actually delivered is something I can check rather than take from the agency's version of it.

So work it through properly. What we paid each of them, what came back, and what happened to any of it after it came back. Take the paid side out of our own books rather than off Renee's summary, because the two have drifted before and I am not signing a second flight on her arithmetic. The handful that made it to closing earned us something on the back end, and I want that in there too, because Grace will ask what the pilot returned and not only what it cost. I do not want a cost per view. I want to know what it cost us to put an actual file on the board, and how much of what came in we were ever in a position to do anything with.

Denise reviewed the pilot content a week or so back and came back with something I have to respect, and Grace put a condition on the money when she released it that limits how I am allowed to commit it. Neither is negotiable, so wherever you land has to survive both.

While you are in there, a piece of what came in was never ours to work and it is still sitting open in the pipeline where the loan officers keep picking it up and burning a morning on it. Close that out so nobody wastes another call, and only that. The live ones stay where they are.

Then the recommendation. Who we keep for the summer, who we let go, and what that spend looks like against what I have been given to spend. If it cuts against Robert, say so and give me the reason I can hand him, because he will ask for one.

Send it up to Grace with Denise copied, put the outcome on the record in the CRM against Cardinal and against each of the five individually, because in September nobody will remember why we passed on the ones we passed on, and come back to Robert in the sales channel so he is not still waiting on me.

rubrics.evidence: See OE 15. The Agent states a total pilot spend of $21,000.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks what was paid to each creator and directs that the paid side be taken from Keystone's own books. The billed total across the sixteen Cardinal bills is the figure that answers it.

rubrics.evidence: See OE 15. The Agent states $7,500 as the pilot cost for @tashatalksmoney.
rubrics.cb_justification: Her true cost is the fact that reframes the whole comparison, since every stakeholder argument in the universe is built on the lower agency-quoted figure.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent determines that Keystone is licensed to originate loans in North Carolina only.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 5. The Agent states the North Carolina only licensing limit.
rubrics.cb_justification: The prompt asks how much of the incoming volume Keystone was ever in a position to act on. That question cannot be answered without the licensing footprint.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent reports that 15 of the 49 leads produced by the creator pilot are located outside North Carolina and cannot be originated by Keystone.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 11 and OE 12. The Agent states that 15 of 49 pilot leads are out of footprint.
rubrics.cb_justification: This is the quantified answer to how much of the delivered volume was workable, and it separates raw lead counts from usable ones.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent reports that 13 of the 18 leads attributed to @tashatalksmoney are located outside North Carolina, leaving 5 that Keystone could work.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 12. The Agent gives the out-of-footprint split for @tashatalksmoney.
rubrics.cb_justification: The creator with the largest apparent delivery is the one whose delivery collapses under the footprint test. This is the central data trap in the task.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent reports that 4 of the 7 loans funded from the creator pilot are attributed to @clthomeguy.
rubrics.evidence: See OE 16 and OE 17. The Agent attributes 4 funded loan(s) to @clthomeguy.
rubrics.cb_justification: Funded files are the outcome Grace states she is measuring on, so attribution of each funded loan to its originating creator is load bearing for the decision.

cases.prompt:
Hey, can you help me close out the First Key creator pilot before this goes to Grace? She's signed off on $6,000 for the next flight and she wants it pointed at conversion this time, not reach. Spring buying season is the window we're aiming at, so this flight has to turn into actual applications rather than followers, and I don't want to hand her a recommendation I can't defend line by line.

We ran three local creators from February through mid April: Bianca Solano at qcfirsthome, Trevor Nakashima at trevorbuyscharlotte, and Priya Raghunathan at charlottehomestart. Each one got their own attribution tag on the leads they sent us, so the lead records should tell us what really landed rather than what anybody claims landed. Those tags are still live on inbound today and the content is still up, so only what landed while the flight was actually running belongs to the pilot. That's my problem with the wrap report the collective sent over. The numbers in it read generously to me, I could never get Bianca's spend to line up cleanly under her name, and not all three were paid the same way either. We have run other things with these creators outside this pilot, so only what was paid for this flight should go into the numbers. Can you work out what we actually paid each creator and what each one actually produced, then get me what we were paying for an impression, an engagement, and a lead that actually converted. I want that last one per creator and not blended, because it's the number Grace will push back on. Count only the ones that reached a funded loan. There's also a content issue I only half know about. Something came up internally about how one of the creators talked about rates and approval odds, and I need to know exactly what was said and by whom before we put any name in a renewal recommendation. The collective quoted renewal pricing for all three, and separately Jordan has been pushing Marisol Vega at clthomehunter and has a price from her, so he needs an answer either way. Grace wants one call, not options.

Once you have all of it, send Grace a recommendation covering the per creator numbers, who we renew for the next flight and on what grounds, what that commitment costs against the $6,000 and what is left uncommitted, and copy Jordan since his creator is in the mix. Whatever that content issue turns out to be, email Denise separately with the specifics, Grace's note only needs the headline. Log the outcome as a note in the CRM against each of the three pilot creators' partner records so the decision and the reasoning are on file and not just sitting in email. And put a note in our sales channel so the team knows which creator content is live and which is on hold, and that nobody reshares anything that is paused.

flags.error_category: Non-Fail - Rubric is agent-centric but does not follow the pattern
flags.auditor_reason: No criterion names an MCP tool and all 60 are framed as actions attributable to the agent, so the failing option does not apply. Twenty-one use the possessive construction "The Agent's email to Grace Yamamoto states..." rather than Agent plus verb plus context, which the spec lists under the non-failing option with valid examples. The remaining thirty-nine follow the pattern directly.

Criterion 19 requires the agent to name Bianca Solano as the creator behind the flagged content while criteria 38, 39 and 40 require that same content attributed to Trevor Nakashima, so no response can satisfy both and criterion 19 must fail every run in which it is graded. The failing option needs two such criteria and the other four recorded fails do not clear the bar: criterion 4 is satisfiable by reporting "39 carry her tag, 34 inside the window", and criterion 22 by narrating the 4,200 quote and its correction, which the verifier justification records the agent doing before failing it anyway.

Five criteria are Incorrect beyond dispute, each contradicting both the data and its own siblings: criterion 4 demands 39 leads for Bianca Solano where the in-window count is 34 and criteria 5 and 6 call 39 wrong in their own evidence; criterion 16 demands 325.00 for Priya Raghunathan where criteria 42 and 49 demand 487.50; criterion 19 names Bianca Solano as the flagged creator off reel FK-R-0402-05 when the flagged reel is FK-R-0416-03, indexed under Trevor and treated as Trevor by six other criteria; criterion 22 demands the 4,200 that criteria 37 and 53 supersede with 4,650; and criterion 51 demands 1,800 uncommitted, impossible beside criterion 37's 4,650 against a 6,000 budget. Reaching the 10 percent threshold required also upholding criterion 9 (CPM 12.37 where the figure is 12.73) and criterion 18 (a "1,200" transfer that is 900), but both are equally readable as non-failing wording errors, and even upholding both gives 6 of 60, or exactly 10.0 percent, which is still non-failing. Minor and not counted: criterion 7 embeds neither the 44 claimed nor the 34 actual, criterion 24's justification restates its own title, criterion 59 exceeds the prompt, and the withholding half of "Grace's note only needs the headline" is untested.
